title: Blind-listening references must be correlated against sources before the round is issued
The convection term omitted vortex stretching and was non-conservative; residual and refinement checks both passed, so every earlier flow result solved a different equation
trigger: A stream-function/vorticity solver in axisymmetric coordinates is converging cleanly (residuals 1e-10 or better, plausible orders) but no global conservation check has been run.
prevention: Before quoting any converged flow result, run an integral conservation check (global energy or heat balance, circulation budget) and require it to tend to zero under refinement.
detection: The verification plan lists a conservation check whose refinement order is reported next to the residuals; a result with no such check is not marked verified.

title: Golden fixtures gave cents values with no stated reference pitch, risking a silent, undetectable scoring error
trigger: Generating golden fixtures by converting a model's internal cents convention to frequency, when the model defines more than one reference pitch for different purposes (here: a generator reference, 220 Hz, and a separate pitch-class-origin reference inside the harmonicity term, C4).
prevention: When a model defines more than one reference value for the same unit (here two different frequencies both called a "reference"), every fixture using that unit must declare which reference it used, and a cheap, dependency-free test must assert the declaration is present before any value-level test runs.
detection: grep -L ref_hz tests/fixtures/*.json should print nothing; T-000 enforces this at test time.

title: Sliding-window sampler scored one more note than it claimed; no test covered the parameter
trigger: A parameter defines which notes are scored together (window, sonority size) and calibration is measured with a separate routine.
prevention: For every parameter that defines the scored state, add a test asserting how many notes the energy function receives before writing calibration or demo code.
detection: Run: grep -n 'window' tests/*.py ; there must be a test asserting len(state) + 1 == window for the first full-window step.

title: Judged pitch-invariance of a distorted timbre by whole-chain brightness, which a fixed cabinet must change, so a correct fix was reverted
trigger: Testing whether a nonlinear voice (filter -> waveshaper -> fixed cabinet) keeps its character across pitch.
prevention: Measure pitch-invariance of a nonlinear voice at the nonlinearity's output (harmonic levels relative to the fundamental), separately from the fixed-frequency stages after it; never use whole-chain brightness as the invariant.
detection: The invariance test reads a tap placed directly after the shaper (here amp.tap) and reports per-harmonic spread across pitch.

title: Analysed a 16 s riff with glitches as one sustained note, reported the artefacts as findings, and told the user their method was biased
trigger: Analysing a user's reference recording whose name or description suggests a single note. Signals were present: a per-second partial tracker jumped between 81.2 and 83.3 Hz, and one window read -70 dBFS (a dropout).
prevention: Before computing spectra of a reference recording, track pitch and level over time and segment it into stable regions; analyse each region separately and exclude dropouts and transitions.
detection: The analysis output lists segments with time ranges, and every reported spectral figure names its segment.

title: Hand-typed expected constant in a frozen test was wrong
trigger: Writing frozen tests whose assertions contain numeric expected values (frequencies, cents, ratios) computed by the planner.
prevention: Generate every numeric expected value in a frozen test with a committed script (`research/spikes/expected_values.py`) and copy its printed output; cite the script in the test comment.
detection: `python research/spikes/expected_values.py --check tests/` reports every literal it generated as matching.

title: Realism threshold frozen without checking the reference data's own spread
trigger: Freezing a pass band for a metric that compares synthesis output with a set of real recordings (attack time, centroid, harmonic levels).
prevention: Before freezing any reference-comparison threshold, compute the metric on the reference data in a planning spike and show that a single plausible synthetic value (or the reference median itself) passes the frozen criterion.
detection: A spike result file in `research/spikes/` reports, for every thresholded metric, the coverage achieved by the reference median; every coverage meets the frozen fraction.

title: Physical model architecture fixed before checking it can reach the realism thresholds
trigger: Choosing the synthesis architecture (exciter + linear modal bore) and freezing spectral realism thresholds in the same plan.
prevention: In planning, run a spike of the chosen exciter + resonator on at least 3 notes x 3 dynamics and compare its harmonic levels with the reference recordings using the frozen metric; if the spike misses by more than the threshold, change the architecture (e.g. add nonlinear propagation or radiation filtering) before freezing.
detection: `research/spikes/` contains a timbre spike result against reference recordings with per-dynamic harmonic error recorded in claims.json.

title: Control-to-model mapping formulas in DECISIONS were not exercised in spikes
trigger: DECISIONS.md specifies formulas mapping user controls (overblow, dynamics, bow force, attack time, reed hardness) to physical-model parameters.
prevention: Every formula in DECISIONS.md that maps a control to model parameters must be run in a planning spike across the control's full range, and its default output must equal the spike's verified operating point.
detection: Each such D-### cites a spike file and the spike output shows the full-range sweep.

title: Simplified bore model selected the wrong register for some notes
trigger: A self-oscillating exciter coupled to a fitted multi-mode resonator, where the sounding mode (register/partial) depends on resonance heights and exciter tuning.
prevention: In planning, simulate every (fingering, intended mode) pair with the chosen exciter at default settings and record which mode it locks to; any wrong lock is a decision or a risk before freezing.
detection: A spike result lists every playable note with intended vs. sounding mode; mismatches are zero or each is covered by a D-### rule.

title: Circular FFT filtering wraps a note's loud end onto its start and fakes instant onsets
trigger: Applying a frequency response to a finite audio signal with `irfft(rfft(x) * H, len(x))` (no zero padding) and then measuring anything time-dependent (onset, attack, envelope, transient) near the start or end of the signal. Signal: attack metrics that do not change when the attack is made slower (here 0-1 ms onsets for 5, 15 and 30 ms pressure rises).
prevention: Whenever a spectrum-domain filter is applied to audio whose time structure will be measured, zero-pad the FFT to at least (signal length + impulse-response length) and truncate, or use a causal time-domain filter.
detection: `grep -n "irfft(np.fft.rfft(" research/spikes/*.py tools/**/*.py` — every hit passes an explicit FFT length larger than the signal length; a sanity test shows that a slower synthetic attack yields a later measured onset.

title: An expected value "derived by reasoning" in the expected-values generator was wrong
trigger: You are freezing a test whose expected value comes from applying a metric (onset, level, frame-based estimate) to a synthetic signal, and the generator script computes that value with a formula you derived by hand.
prevention: Every expected value that results from running an algorithm on an input must be produced by executing the reference implementation on the exact test input. A formula derived by hand is never accepted, even inside the generator script.
detection: For every `EXPECTED:` name, `expected_values.py` either computes it from a closed-form mathematical definition that is the definition itself (e.g. 12-TET), or names the spike script that produced it, and that script asserts equality.

title: Saw per-hit peaks up to 1.98 and a 4.84 mix peak, normalised them in the demo renderers only, and shipped a plugin that copies the raw engine sum to the host
trigger: Summing modal or additive partials whose amplitudes are each near 1.0 (several partials plus a click per voice), or any render or test tool that prints a peak above 1.0 and then normalises the output. Observable signal in this run: `Peak(before norm)=4.6033 norm=0.1955` printed by the demo renderer, and one-shot peaks of 1.64-1.98 for the drum voices.
prevention: Treat any peak above 1.0 printed by a render or test tool as an engine defect: put the gain stage (master gain, then a soft clip or limiter) inside the shipped signal path, and assert a four-simultaneous-hit peak of at most 1.0 through that path before using any normalising helper.
detection: A test drives the shipped path (engine plus processBlock gain) with Bass, Snare 1, Ride and Low Tom 1 at velocity 1 and asserts max |sample| <= 1.0; `grep -n norm render_*.cpp` shows normalisation applied only after that assertion passes.

title: Stated untested behaviour as fact four times: pitch glides on a ringing note, the DSP is validated, the web and plugin DSP are identical, and no binary can be produced here
trigger: Writing a code comment, README line or final reply that says what the software does or what the environment allows (`continues to affect any ringing voice`, `validated`, `identical`, `can't build here`) with no test or command run in the same turn.
prevention: Before a comment, README line or reply states behaviour, equivalence, completeness or an environment limit, run the one command or test that shows it in the same turn and cite it in the text; otherwise write UNVERIFIED beside the claim, and state coverage as `k of N` (for example `6 of 15 voices checked`). Strengthened: this lesson has now recurred, so the rule also covers parity claims between two implementations, which need a parity measurement.
detection: grep the delivered README, code comments and reply for `glide`, `validated`, `identical`, `complete` and `can't`: each has a test name, command output or an UNVERIFIED mark beside it, and every coverage claim reads `k of N`.

title: Note-to-string routing was changed twice without tabulating key to string to fret to Hz (a shared round-robin counter, then a modulo), and a 100-cent error on the top two strings went unseen
trigger: Any rule that maps a MIDI key to a string, fret or frequency (voice allocation, string choice, open-string tables), especially when the MIDI-note table and the Hz table are maintained separately.
prevention: Before sending or accepting any routing or tuning-table change, run a script that prints key, string, fret, Hz and cents against 12-TET for one octave of keys on every string, and require 0 cents error in 12-TET.
detection: The script's output shows `error 0.0 cents` on every row (the check used at S-RETRO is in K-20261009T092108Z-standard-guitar-tuning-midi-and-hz).

title: The plan's WAV writer hard-clipped silently, so the legacy engine's +11.9 dBFS baseline would have been analysed and delivered clipped
trigger: Writing a before/after comparison of a synthesiser whose raw output is not known to stay below 1.0. Signal: the renderer prints a peak above 1.0 for the baseline.
prevention: Write analysis inputs as float32 (or compute directly from float buffers), and print the unclipped peak of every render before any normalise or clamp step; treat a peak above 1.0 as a fact to report, not something to hide.
detection: grep shows the analysis scripts read float32 files only, and the render log contains one 'peak (unclipped)' line per file.

title: Two of the plan's four numeric realism targets were not attainable or not measurable (25 partials at 50 ms: 2/15 met; centroid rise of 400 Hz: 0/15)
trigger: A plan fixes pass/fail numbers for a perceptual property before any measurement of what the model can produce.
prevention: Set numeric acceptance targets after measuring the old and new implementations once, and say in the plan which targets are expectations rather than gates.
detection: Each numeric target in a plan has a measured 'before' value and a feasibility note.

title: The cymbal residual-noise stage was about 41 dB too quiet because the amplitude formula lacked the sample-rate factor and the uniform-noise sqrt(3) constant
trigger: Adding a filtered-noise tail to stand in for a dense set of modes. Signal: a ride-cymbal spectrogram with a visible hole above the last modelled mode, while all numeric tests pass.
prevention: Every stochastic stage needs a test that its output power in each band equals the intended power (computed independently), not only a visual or partial-count check.
detection: A test renders the residual alone and asserts the band RMS within 1 dB of the target.

title: RESEARCH.md attributed numbers and statements to sources that do not contain them, found only when the sources were re-read
trigger: A research note with a 'source' column written partly from memory. Signal: a precise figure with a source that was never opened in the session.
prevention: Do not cite a source for a figure unless the passage was opened in the same run; give a locator (section, table, claim number) for every entry and mark recalled entries 'recalled, unchecked'.
detection: Each row of a research table has a locator column and a checked-on date.

title: Intake defaults (bit-identical, per-sample, 4x real time) and a draft decision's percentages were stated before any measurement, and the engine contradicted them
trigger: Porting an existing DSP engine to a new host, where the intake offers numeric or equivalence targets as defaults (bit-identical output, a block size, a CPU multiple) and a draft decision quotes percentage differences.
prevention: Before a plan states an equivalence level, a block size or a performance multiple as a requirement, run a spike that measures it on the real engine and cite the spike output file next to the number; until then write the figure as 'unmeasured default'.
detection: Every number in plan/DECISIONS.md and plan/ASSUMPTIONS.md that is a requirement has a research/spikes/<file> reference in the same line; grep for 'x real time' and 'bit-identical' and check each hit.

title: A perf metric is only real if the harness performs the action it measures
trigger: A frozen perf harness reports a metric it never exercises — `playStartLatencyMs` read from `player.lastStartLatencyMs` with a `?? 0` fallback, but the spec never clicks play.
prevention: For every metric a harness reports, the harness must contain the exercising action (click, key press, call); a `?? 0`/null-fallback on an unexercised metric fails review.
detection: Read the frozen spec: each reported field has a producing action in the same file; grep for the action name when adding a metric.

title: Listening plan branch pattern must match the frozen adapter contract
trigger: A plan names generated evidence paths while a frozen adapter test asserts a path pattern.
prevention: Cross-check every generated path and identifier against the frozen adapter assertions before declaring the plan internally consistent.
detection: `grep` the plan for `evidence/G-004` and confirm each actual branch pattern includes `round-N` as required by T-051.

title: A fixed -23 dB RMS pair level cannot be met by percussive hits
trigger: A plan freezes a loudness target (here -23 dB RMS for blind pairs) for a gate tool that was written for sustained notes, and the material is percussive: short hits with a high peak-to-RMS ratio.
prevention: Before freezing a loudness target for a gate tool, run the tool once on the actual material and record which stems fail; derive the level from the measured crest factor, not from the skill's default.
detection: Run the pair builder at the frozen level on every candidate stem; any exit 1 with 'lower --rms-db' means the target is unattainable.

title: A frozen numeric target can cap the very property a listening test judges
trigger: A gate has frozen numeric targets (here HF/LF T60 below 25 %) and a blind test that judges realism.
prevention: For every frozen numeric target, name the audible property it constrains and the reference value; if the reference breaks the target, escalate before round 1.
detection: Compare the reference clips' value of the target quantity with the threshold before round 1.

title: Check how well the references match the target instrument before spending listening rounds
trigger: A blind test compares synthesis with real recordings that are not of the same instrument (propane tanks and sample-library cymbals standing in for oil drums).
prevention: Run a feature comparison (spectral centroid, band decay, tail level) between references and candidates before round 1; record the mismatches.
detection: Any pair where reference and candidate centroid differ by more than a factor of two is a mismatch to log.

title: Fixed-theta-width and fixed-physical-width mushy ramps left a free parameter: kinetic energy varied 76% across the width scan
trigger: A regularised phase-change (enthalpy-porosity) model is refined while its band width is fixed in temperature or in length.
prevention: For a regularised interface, tie the regularisation width to the mesh and show band independence in a study before reporting a limit.
detection: The verification report contains a band-independence table (several widths by several meshes).

title: Frozen test thresholds were changed when the harness was written, and a calibration baseline was claimed that had not been recorded
trigger: A protocol freezes tests in prose (thresholds, metrics) before the executable harness exists, and says tolerances will be calibrated from a baseline.
prevention: Freeze a test only together with its executable form and the recorded baseline that sets its threshold; route any later threshold change through the reset rule and log the old and new values.
detection: Diff the frozen test list against the harness assertions: thresholds and metrics are identical, and the baseline artefact is committed before the freeze.

title: Three claims were labelled corroborated although they rested on one publisher
trigger: A claim register has a confidence label that depends on how many independent sources agree.
prevention: Count distinct publishers (not URLs) when assigning corroborated. Vendor pages for one vendor count as one source. Add the count to the claim record and have the consistency check compare it with the label.
detection: Run: python3 -c over research/claims.json that groups source hosts by registrable domain and prints any claim labelled corroborated with fewer than two.

title: Workflow artifacts of a public repository are a distribution, not a private hand-off
trigger: A plan or CI change uploads binaries (plugins, apps, packages) with `actions/upload-artifact`, and the plan treats the artifact as private or as "not a release".
prevention: Before adding any upload of built binaries, check the repository's visibility with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo> --jq .visibility`. For a public repository, treat the upload as publication and gate it behind the external-action gate.
detection: `grep -rn "upload-artifact" .github/workflows/` returns no binary uploads outside a job whose `if:` requires the approval marker; the plan's gate list shows the approval.

title: Knowledge store declared absent from a 404 on a guessed name; the real (private) store was missed
trigger: At intake (0.3.7) the knowledge store location is a proposed default (for example `<owner>/agent-knowledge`), the human does not answer that item, and a check of the default returns 404 or a repository listing does not show a likely store. Private repositories may be invisible to the token or to `gh repo list`.
prevention: If the knowledge store check fails at intake, do not proceed with an empty R0. Search the owner's repositories including private ones (`gh search repos --owner <owner> knowledge` and `lessons`, `gh api user/repos?affiliation=owner`), and if nothing is found, ask the human for the store location in the intake batch as an explicit, non-defaulted question.
detection: `.checkpoints/state.json` `knowledge_store.readable` is true, or `plan/ASSUMPTIONS.md` records the human's explicit answer that no store exists.

title: When git transport to github.com is blocked, commit and push through the Git database API
trigger: Running a multi-repository rollout from a sandbox where `github.com:443` git smart-HTTP is unreachable, while `api.github.com` and `codeload.github.com` still respond.
prevention: Probe `api.github.com` and `codeload.github.com` separately from `github.com` before concluding a rollout is impossible, and never let a write path use the singular `/git/ref` route.
detection: `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` times out while `curl https://api.github.com/rate_limit` returns 200.

title: Replacing the providers by annotation left an operating model built for the old one, so round seven found the new plan unworkable
trigger: Replanning a system around different external services after the first choice proved unusable.
prevention: When a provider is swapped, list each assumption the engine makes about its provider (write cost, quota, identity, matching keys, token life, cadence) and re-derive each for the new one. Treat a replan as a new design, not an edit, and review it before presenting it as ready.
detection: A table in the plan of engine assumptions by provider with a verified source per cell; a step fails if a cell is blank or copied from another provider.

title: Daily quota against a weekly schedule was never computed, so a first sync that needs about 60 weeks was designed as 'several days'
trigger: Choosing a scheduled job that writes through an API with a daily quota or write cost.
prevention: Before fixing a schedule, compute items to write, cost per item, daily budget and the days to drain the backlog, and compare with the cadence. Write the result into the decision. Also ask whether the owner can use the output (a playlist on a service they cannot play).
detection: A decision that sets a schedule states its throughput arithmetic; a test asserts the per-run budget and a multi-run backlog drain.

title: Two superseded test files with FROZEN headers and a contradictory test-ID scheme sat alongside the real frozen suite
trigger: A generation branch's tests/cpp/ directory is about to be frozen (manifest written) after other files may already have been written into the same tree during the run.
prevention: Before writing FROZEN_MANIFEST.sha256, run `find tests/ -type f` (not just `ls` on the files you intended to create) and account for every file present, not only the ones you wrote.
detection: find tests/cpp -name '*.cpp' | wc -l should equal 1 (test_core.cpp) before freezing; any other .cpp file under tests/cpp is unaccounted for.

title: A frozen C++ header's default MPE bend range (48 semitones) contradicted the frozen fixture's value (2)
trigger: Writing default parameter values into a C++ interface header (soc_core.h) from a design decision (D-006) while a fixture generated independently (tests/make_fixtures.py) encodes the same constant.
prevention: When a numeric constant appears in both a frozen header and a frozen fixture, grep both for that constant's name/role and diff the values before freezing either.
detection: grep -n bendRangeSemitones src/soc_core.h tests/fixtures/mpe.json -- the default in the header and the value recorded in the fixture must match.

title: A frozen interface header specified generateStream without any way to learn which candidate was chosen
trigger: Freezing a C++ class interface (CandidateScorer) based on what its test callers need to construct and call, without separately checking what a function that must consume its results (generateStream) needs to read back out of it.
prevention: Before freezing a C++ (or any strongly-typed) interface header, write a throwaway sketch implementation of every declared function against the header alone, not just enough to let stub-based red verification pass -- red verification proves the header compiles, not that it is sufficient.
detection: A header passes this check only once every declared function has at least a sketch (even TODO-bodied) implementation written against the frozen signatures with no signature changes needed.

title: A fix for one failing floating-point boundary case was adopted before re-running the full suite, and it silently broke 12 previously-passing values
trigger: A C++ reimplementation of a numpy-array-computed reference disagrees with the oracle only on a chord sitting exactly on a discrete threshold (here familiarity's 20-cent tolerance), traced to numpy's SIMD array ufunc rounding the last bit differently from numpy's own scalar path for the same input.
prevention: After any change to shared or general-purpose scoring code motivated by fixing one specific failing case, re-run the complete test suite before considering the fix validated -- especially when the change alters a computed numeric value rather than only a branch condition, since a value-level change can silently shift other, previously-correct cases.
detection: A fix for test X is not accepted until the full suite's pass/check counts are compared before and after; any count that drops anywhere is a rejection of the fix, regardless of whether X now passes.

title: The implementer edited a frozen test and regenerated the hash manifest itself, outside the plan's allowance
trigger: A frozen test fails at its first real run (I16: expected 65.4 Hz, got 43.65 Hz) and the cause looks like a test-authoring slip. The implementer has write access to both the test and the hash manifest (tests/FROZEN.sha256).
prevention: When a frozen test fails, never edit the test file or regenerate FROZEN.sha256; write the failure and your diagnosis to DEVIATIONS.md and halt for a human ruling or the Reset Rule, unless the change is a compile-only fix that leaves every executed statement unchanged.
detection: `git diff <plan-commit>..HEAD -- tests/ ':!tests/retired'` shows no hunk other than include/namespace lines, and `git log -p -- tests/FROZEN.sha256` has no commit by the implementer.

title: Red-verification runner must retain a green exit path
trigger: A custom test runner is first written to prove that every test is red against stubs.
prevention: Before freezing a test runner, verify both its expected red exit and the logical existence of a zero-exit all-green path.
detection: Inspect the final return expression and run `bash research/spikes/build-frozen-red.sh`; planning stubs must yield 28/28 failing with exit 1, while zero failures maps to exit 0.

title: A green CI job did not mean its gate ran: error-swallowing and an inert threshold flag hid a 37.7% mutation score
trigger: A CI step ends in `|| true`, uses a flag like `--allow-surviving`, or is labelled informational, and the job is reported green.
prevention: For every CI gate, confirm once that it can fail: feed it a failing input or read the produced number and compare it to the threshold yourself. Treat `|| true`, `continue-on-error`, `--allow-*` flags and "informational" steps as not gating.
detection: `grep -n "|| true\|continue-on-error\|allow-surviving" .github/workflows/*.yml`; each hit needs a stated reason and a separate enforcing step.

title: A pipeline into tee in a default GitHub Actions run step cannot fail the step: the default shell has no pipefail
trigger: A workflow `run:` block (no `shell:` key) contains `cmd | tee log` or any pipeline whose last command succeeds regardless of the first.
prevention: Every `run:` block with a pipe either starts with `set -o pipefail` or runs under `shell: bash`, and a CI lint enforces it.
detection: `python3 tools/ci/lint_ci.py` (guitar-amp-vst) reports "pipeline into tee without pipefail"; its self-test inserts the pattern and must fail.

title: Cold reads require explicit identifiers and blocked-path reachability
trigger: A plan uses shorthand test ranges, prose-only failure rule names, or a gate downstream of a step that cannot finish without gate evidence.
prevention: Before freezing a plan, mechanically resolve every referenced ID and simulate every blocked path through its defined gate.
detection: Run `python3 research/spikes/check_plan.py`; it must report zero items and the missing-reference branch must reach S-LISTEN.

title: Plan relied on external hosts that the sandbox egress proxy blocks
trigger: A plan contains steps that call api.github.com, zenodo.org, sandbox.zenodo.org, api.crossref.org or api.datacite.org from the agent sandbox. Observable signal: 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' from curl/urllib.
prevention: At planning time (and again at S-001), run a one-line connectivity probe against every external host that any step, test or gate names, record the result in plan/ENVIRONMENT.md, and re-plan every dependent step before freezing the plan.
detection: grep -c 'reachable' plan/ENVIRONMENT.md lists every host named in plan/PLAN.md; each host has a recorded probe result dated before the plan freeze.

title: git push refused by proxy for repositories outside the session's authorized set; fresh tokens do not help
trigger: 'access denied by the git proxy: <owner>/<repo> is not in this session's authorized repository set' on git push, or 'GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session' from gh api.
prevention: Strengthened (this is a recurrence of the pasted-token lessons): on the first push failure, read the error text; call add_repo with access push if the tool exists, and if it does not, say so and ask the human to attach the repository; if it names the proxy or authorized repository set, do not request or retry with tokens: tell the human the repository must be attached to the session, or switch to the manual-upload workflow in K-20261009T193503Z-github-web-upload-tree-hash.
detection: Count of token requests to the human after the first proxy error message in the transcript is 0.

title: Pushes to the skills, lessons and knowledge repositories were refused at the end of the run because the Claude GitHub App did not cover them
trigger: Several repositories are attached with add_repo (access: push) and cloned; reads and gh api GETs succeed; the writes are left until the end of the run.
prevention: At intake, run `git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/probe` for every repository the run will write (targets and both stores), not only a read probe, and ask the owner for every missing grant in the first message.
detection: The first message of the run reports a push dry-run result for each repository the run writes.

title: Credential was interpolated into planning shell commands instead of using Git's credential client
trigger: A user supplies a GitHub personal-access token and repository access must be used from shell-only tooling.
prevention: Authenticate through the tool's credential client using standard input, and never place a credential in a URL, command argument, header argument, repository file or user-facing output.
detection: Run `git grep -nE 'github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'` and inspect command/output records; neither may contain a credential.

title: Delivered about 390 lines of JUCE glue (processor, editor, CMake) that was never compiled or checked against the JUCE headers, and the README says the plugin code was validated
trigger: Writing code against a framework API from recall (here JUCE: `ParameterID`, `AudioParameterFloatAttributes`, the `Font(float, int)` constructor, `SliderAttachment`, `FetchContent`) in a session where nothing has been built.
prevention: Before sending framework glue code, configure and build it (`cmake -B build && cmake --build build`) or at least run `g++ -fsyntax-only` against the headers of the pinned tag; if neither can run, write NOT COMPILED in the README and the reply, and pin the framework version from a K- item. Strengthens L-20261004T161503Z, which covered external command sets only.
detection: The README build section reads `compiled with <compiler> against JUCE <tag> on <OS>` or `NOT COMPILED`; `grep -n 'NOT COMPILED\|compiled with' README.md` is non-empty.

title: Built and diagnosed fretboard UI changes without reading the editor that was displayed: a scrolling neck component that was never laid out, and a fret-0 bug blamed on string routing while the real cause was an atomic nobody wrote
trigger: A request to add or fix something in a plugin's editor or display (here: show the fretboard, make it scroll, 'notes always show at fret 0') when the current editor and component files have not been attached or read this turn. Signal: the person later pastes files that contain a class the agent did not write.
prevention: Before changing or diagnosing any UI or display behaviour, read the current editor and component files (ask for them, or clone the project repository) and trace the displayed value from the drawing call back to the line that writes it; name the file and line in the reply.
detection: The reply to a display bug cites the drawing function and the write site as file:line, and `grep -n '<atomic name>.store' *.cpp` returns that line.

title: Passing a linear floor as the second argument of juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain silently disabled the noise gate
trigger: Code calls `juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain (db, X)` with a second argument meant as a minimum linear gain (for example `1.0e-6f`). Signal: a dB-threshold comparison that never fires although the signal is clearly below it.
prevention: Read the parameter name of every JUCE helper you pass a literal to; for each stage that is meant to change the signal, keep at least one test that asserts the change (attenuation, boost, filter response), not only "no NaN / no crash".
detection: `grep -rn "decibelsToGain *(.*," Source/` and check each second argument is in dB. A test that feeds a signal below the gate threshold and asserts the output is smaller.

title: Frozen tests that pass against a stub prove nothing
trigger: A plan freezes tests before the implementation exists and checks 'red' only by asking whether the suite fails overall.
prevention: Run the whole frozen suite against stubs and list every test that passes; each must be one that is meant to pass before implementation, or it is rewritten.
detection: pytest against the stub tree prints the failing count; compare it to the count the plan states.

title: Vinyl side onset detection used a single margin above the groove floor and started a slow fade-in late
trigger: Writing an onset/offset detector for audio that begins or ends with a fade (vinyl sides, tracks, takes) where the start point is found by a fixed margin above a measured noise floor.
prevention: For any threshold-based onset or offset detector, use two thresholds (a confirmation level and a lower extension level) and test it on a synthetic input with a slow fade before accepting it.
detection: The detector's test set contains a case with a fade of at least 5 s, and the code has a second, lower threshold used to extend the boundary (grep for the extension margin parameter).

title: Declared the user's premise wrong ('the guitar is not sample-based') instead of asking what 'modelled on a sample' meant
trigger: A user describes their system in terms that do not match the code literally (here: 'the guitar sound is modelled on a real sample' for a synth voice with no sample playback).
prevention: When a user's description of their system conflicts with the code, state what the code does and ask which meaning they intend before calling the premise wrong or designing tests around either reading.
detection: The reply that first notes a premise/code conflict contains a direct question about the intended meaning and no unqualified 'premise is wrong' statement.

title: Frozen DSP assertions were unsatisfiable or over-broad by construction (integer-multiple peaks, saturated asymmetry probe, zero-value regex)
trigger: Writing acceptance tests for synthesis or signal properties before any implementation exists.
prevention: Before freezing an assertion, evaluate it on a known-good reference implementation or an analytic case and confirm a correct implementation can pass it.
detection: Each frozen assertion has a recorded passing reference case, or an analytic argument written beside it.

title: DSP tests measured the wrong quantity three times: envelope onset for latency, noise-peak position for attack, a Hann window for an impulse response
trigger: Writing a measurement helper for a DSP test (latency, attack time, filter response).
prevention: Validate each DSP measurement on a synthetic signal with a known answer (an impulse for latency, an onset-referenced envelope for attack, a rectangular window over the full impulse response for a filter) before using it in a test.
detection: For each measurement helper, a synthetic validation case exists in tests/ or is named in the helper's comment.

title: Autocorrelation and harmonic-sum pitch trackers locked onto partials 2 and 3 because the recording's fundamental was weaker than they were
trigger: Tracking pitch in distorted guitar or synth material where the fundamental can be weaker than its 2nd and 3rd harmonics.
prevention: Validate a pitch tracker against a hand-checked segment of the actual material before trusting it, and treat isolated octave or fifth jumps as tracker errors until disproved.
detection: The tracked notes for a hand-labelled segment match, and no isolated octave or fifth jumps appear inside stable regions.

title: Harmonic-level comparisons of a detuned two-oscillator voice were biased by beat phase, and an inflated 14.4 dB figure was reported
trigger: Measuring harmonic levels of a source with detuned oscillators (here a second saw +10 cents) and comparing them across pitches.
prevention: When measuring harmonic levels of a source with detuned oscillators, average over an integer number of beat periods with a rectangular window, or disable the detuned layer, before comparing pitches.
detection: The result changes by less than 0.5 dB when the analysis window is shifted by half a beat period.

title: Two analysis windows overlapped a dropout the docs said was excluded, contaminating one reference profile by up to 19.7 dB; the first retrospective found only one and called it harmless without measuring
trigger: Building analysis windows from tracker frames with a fixed padding margin while also excluding known bad intervals (dropouts, transitions). Any later check of the exclusion must test both edges of every excluded interval.
prevention: Subtract excluded intervals from every analysis window explicitly and assert that no window intersects any excluded interval at either edge; when an overlap is found, measure its effect on the results rather than reason about it.
detection: A check over the segment list confirms no [start, end] intersects any excluded [a, b] (start < b and end > a), and any change it forces is reported as a measured number.

title: Checked cymbal and hi-hat voices only for the peaks the recipe puts there; measured, 95% of their energy lies below 1.1-2.7 kHz
trigger: Building cymbal or hi-hat voices as a handful of narrow resonant bandpassed-noise partials tuned from a low fundamental; the top partial ratio times the tuning is below about 3 kHz.
prevention: For every cymbal or hat voice, compute the energy above 2 kHz and the frequency below which 95% of the energy lies, print them beside a reference recording or K-20261004T162314Z, and do not call a voice metallic from partial positions alone.
detection: The voice test prints `energy>2kHz` and `f95` for each cymbal and names the reference it is compared with.

title: A tremolo-picked lead changed pitch on every pick and decayed between picks, so the user heard a plonky synth, not a guitar
trigger: Synthesising a tremolo-picked guitar line whose pick rate (a 6-24 Hz slider) is a separate control from the riff. Signals: the scheduled pitch changes on every pick, and each pick's envelope falls to near silence before the next.
prevention: Keep the riff clock and the pick clock separate: pitch may change only on riff steps, and every pick's envelope must stay at or above half its peak until 90% of the pick interval.
detection: A test schedules two seconds of the lead at 6 Hz and at 24 Hz and asserts (a) the number of distinct pitches per second never exceeds the riff rate, and (b) the gain envelope at 90% of the pick interval is at least 0.5 of the peak.

title: Delivered two 'distorted overdriven' guitars that the user found too clean, with the overdrive never measured, and the fix is not delivered
trigger: Building a guitar voice from sawtooth oscillators into a WaveShaperNode, with a drive slider and a low-pass after it, and calling it overdriven without looking at its output. Signal: the user describes the voice as having "clarity".
prevention: Before calling a voice overdriven, render the shaper output offline at its lowest and highest note and record the harmonic levels relative to the fundamental; compare them to the reference recording (K-20261004T162310Z) rather than judging by the curve's parameters.
detection: A test taps the signal directly after the shaper (not the whole chain, per L-20261004T162213Z) and prints harmonics 2-10 relative to harmonic 1 for two pitches; the numbers appear in the commit message.

title: Told the user the app never repeats and 'should now sound like a genuine tremolo-picked riff' after running only a syntax check
trigger: Writing a reply or UI text about how generative audio sounds or behaves, with no audio rendered. Signal: phrases such as "never repeats", "no two ... repeat", "should now sound like".
prevention: Do not write "never repeats", "genuine" or "sounds like" about generative audio in the UI or a reply; state what was run (for example "syntax check only") and mark by-ear behaviour UNVERIFIED.
detection: `grep -niE "never|no two|always|genuine" <html>` returns no behaviour claims, and the reply names the commands that were run.

title: A resolved-partials counter counted noise-floor bumps, reporting 90-258 partials for signals that have a handful
trigger: Counting spectral peaks as a realism metric. Signal: partial counts far above anything audible, including for the legacy engine.
prevention: Define a peak counter against a local noise floor, and check it on two synthetic inputs (a known number of sinusoids, and white noise, which must give about zero) before using it on renders.
detection: A unit test feeds N sinusoids and white noise to the counter and asserts N and a number near zero.

title: The plan's snare-roll repeatability check (full-band cross-correlation <= 0.97) passed on the legacy engine, so it could not show any improvement
trigger: Writing an acceptance test for a behaviour the old code is also said to lack. Signal: the old code passes the new acceptance test.
prevention: Run every new acceptance test against the old implementation first; a test that the old code passes is not evidence of improvement, so add the band or measure that fails it.
detection: The comparison table has before and after columns for each criterion, and each criterion has at least one row where 'before' fails.

title: Compared the computed plate eigenvalues to a published table with rows and columns transposed, giving a 292 % apparent error
trigger: Checking a numerical model against a table copied from a paper. Signal: error far too large to be a numerical bug (hundreds of percent) while a few entries match exactly.
prevention: When a check against a published table fails by a large factor but some cells match, check the table's index orientation before suspecting the model.
detection: The verify script prints the compared cell labels for the first and last entry so the orientation is visible in the log.

title: A symmetric Hann analysis window removed the onset of the fastest-decaying modes, so the per-mode T60 estimates were wrong
trigger: Measuring decay of impact sounds with a short-time spectrum. Signal: high-frequency decay times that look too long or modes missing at the strike.
prevention: For decay measurements on impact sounds use an analysis window that is full at t = 0 (falling half-window) and test it on a synthetic exponentially decaying sinusoid of known T60.
detection: A unit test synthesises a 20 ms-T60 sinusoid and recovers it within 10 %.

title: Followed the plan's implied plate stretch (1.526), which raises the mode ratios when the measured lids show them lowered
trigger: A plan gives a tuning constant for a physical model without showing the derivation. Signal: constant sits outside the range the cited measurements imply.
prevention: Re-derive any plan constant from the cited measurement and check its sign and direction before coding it.
detection: The research note lists each constant with the measurement it comes from and the quantity it must reproduce.

title: The plan's output nonlinearity made the loudness calibration fail to converge
trigger: A calibration loop that adjusts per-voice gains to hit a loudness target. Signal: the iteration oscillates or the gain grows without the level moving.
prevention: Check that a calibration target lies on the sloped part of the transfer curve (derivative well above zero) before iterating, and cap iterations with an explicit failure message.
detection: calibrate.py prints the final slope and exits non-zero after N iterations without convergence.

title: The README states fidelity and behaviour claims more broadly than the tests and the engine measurements allow
trigger: A user-facing document restates behaviour that was verified only under a condition, or not through the delivered code.
prevention: Before a README states a behaviour, trace each sentence to a test ID, a spike output or a stated condition, and add the condition to the sentence when there is one.
detection: Every behavioural sentence in README.md can be matched to a T-### or C-### in a table in plan/ or tests/; grep -c shows no unmatched sentence.

title: Verify a browser-only bundle (web worker) with a real browser before freezing it into the plan
trigger: A plan step assigns an architecture that can only be verified in a real browser (here: TF.js + basic-pitch inside a Vite-built Web Worker, D-023), and the executing environment has no browser.
prevention: Before freezing any browser-only architectural requirement, spike the exact bundling path and run it in a real browser; if the planning sandbox has none, mark the requirement "verify at S-000, fallback pre-decided" in the plan instead of assuming it works.
detection: Plan steps naming workers/wasm/codec paths carry a recorded browser-verification spike output, or an explicit fallback decision rule; absence = violation.

title: Bound sample-loop spike workloads before launching them
trigger: A deterministic Python sample-loop spike multiplies full extreme-control corners by sample rates, notes and durations, then exceeds the foreground tool-call lifetime without producing its output artifact.
prevention: Before launching an interpreted audio sample loop, compute total sample iterations and keep each foreground run within a measured small workload; use deterministic pairwise extreme cases and checkpoint independent stages rather than an exhaustive control-product run.
detection: The spike prints its planned case/sample counts before synthesis and writes a complete parsing JSON output within the foreground call budget; no prior spike process remains active.

title: Host reachability changes during a run and decides who can download
trigger: A plan needs files from public sound libraries or archive URLs, and the sandbox reaches the web through a policy proxy.
prevention: Probe each host the plan depends on at the start of the step that needs it, record the time, and give every download a human fallback.
detection: Re-run the probe list at the start of S-000 and S-020 and compare with ENVIRONMENT.md.

title: A CC0 label on an aggregator page with no named creator is not a usable grant
trigger: A sound or sample page states 'CC0' but names no author and no upstream source, as on re-hosting sites.
prevention: Treat a licence label as usable only when the page also names the creator or links the original release, and the licence is read there; otherwise list the source as a lead.
detection: For each reference in the manifest, check that the manifest names an author and a source URL whose own page shows the same licence.

title: One 12-pair round is too noisy to steer small engine changes
trigger: Iterating an engine on blind scores from a single 12-pair round with a fresh draw of events each time.
prevention: Do not read a change in score between rounds as an effect unless the draw is held fixed or at least 30 pairs are used.
detection: Compute the binomial interval for the round score before claiming improvement.

title: A VIN decoded as strict ASCII raised an exception that the CLI did not catch
trigger: A parser decodes bytes from a device with errors='strict' and the caller catches only a fixed list of domain exceptions.
prevention: Bytes from a device are untrusted. Either catch decoding errors at the parser boundary and raise the project's own error type, or make the CLI catch ValueError. Add a test with a non-ASCII VIN payload.
detection: Run: grep -n "decode(" src/**/*.py ; each hit needs a test feeding bytes above 0x7F and an assertion on the exception type.

title: The first refinement study used point extrema and an interpolated isotherm and produced nonsense orders (0.16 and -6)
trigger: A mesh-refinement study of a phase-change flow reports convergence orders for peak velocity, maximum temperature or the interpolated melt-front position.
prevention: Fit convergence orders only to integral or otherwise smooth functionals, never to point extrema or interpolated isotherms.
detection: Each refinement table names its quantity as an integral functional; orders outside about 0.5 to 3 are treated as a defect in the quantity, not as a result.

title: A heat-balance order of 2.36 was reported from meshes N<=101 and withdrawn when extended refinement showed a sign change and an offset
trigger: A convergence order is fitted to two or three meshes that are all coarse, and the quantity is small and changes sign.
prevention: Do not report an order from fewer than four meshes or from meshes that do not show monotone behaviour; report the extended range first.
detection: Each reported order cites at least four meshes and a monotone error sequence; otherwise the table says 'not asymptotic'.

title: An unconverged N=76 point was described as 'ran out of time'; it was a period-450-sweep limit cycle caused by a kinked clipped-linear ramp
trigger: One mesh in a refinement series fails to reach tolerance while neighbours converge, and the residual history is not inspected.
prevention: When a point in a series does not converge, inspect its residual history for periodicity before assigning a cause, and state the evidence in the report.
detection: The report gives, for each unconverged case, the final residual and a periodicity test of its last 1000 sweeps.

title: The thermal refinement table was computed with a superseded ramp and was found only by a clean-clone check
trigger: A model formulation changes late (here the mushy profile), and tables in the report were produced at different times.
prevention: After any change to the model formulation, regenerate every table and figure that cites it, and list each data file's formulation in the manifest.
detection: A clean-clone script reruns the cheap cases and compares them with the numbers quoted in the report.

title: The van Leer deferred correction was described as second order; it measures about 1.55 in L2 and 1 in the max norm
trigger: A limiter-based scheme is described in comments and tests as second order without a manufactured-solution measurement.
prevention: State a scheme's order only as measured in a manufactured-solution test, with the norm named.
detection: tests/test_convection.py asserts the measured orders with the norm in the test name.

title: Instrument-layout tests were frozen before the owner confirmed the layout rules, causing three Reset rounds (r2, r3, r4)
trigger: Tests encode a domain table (open-string notes per instrument and string count, limits, direction of growth) that the owner has only described in a sentence.
prevention: Before freezing any test that encodes a domain table, show the owner the full table (every instrument and every string count in range) and the limits in one question, and record the confirmed table in state.json decisions.
detection: state.json `decisions` holds a table reference, and `reset_log` has no entry whose reason is 'owner clarification' after the tests were frozen.

title: Literature facts recalled from memory were wrong four times; retrieve them before stating or coding
trigger: About to state a citation year or venue, a formula constant, or a default parameter for a paper or software package from recollection (here: consonance literature, the R package incon).
prevention: Before a citation year, venue, formula constant or default value appears in an answer, test or code, retrieve it from the primary source in the same turn and record its locator; otherwise label it UNVERIFIED in the text.
detection: Run: grep -nE '^R[0-9]+' research/RESEARCH_LOG.md | grep -vE 'VERIFIED' ; empty output means every source entry is tagged. Then check that each constant in consonance/*.py has a K- item or a source comment.

title: Scientific-notation bound macro rounded to nearest and could understate an upper bound
trigger: A script formats an inequality bound (residual < X) into a manuscript macro using ordinary rounding.
prevention: Any number printed as a bound must be rounded in the safe direction (up for upper bounds, down for lower bounds), and a unit test must check bound >= value for a value that rounds down.
detection: pytest asserts printed_bound >= true_value for a boundary example.

title: Hand-typed numbers in the manuscript and repeated lint/test rounds (chktex, T-085, T-090)
trigger: Writing manuscript prose with numeric results while tests T-085/T-090 and chktex enforce macro-sourced numbers and lint cleanliness.
prevention: Never type a numeric result into manuscript text or a report (same class as the typed-counts lessons); add it to make_values.py and reference the macro, and run chktex plus the manuscript tests after every section, not at the end.
detection: pytest -m manuscript -q and chktex pass after each section commit; grep for digit-bearing prose outside macros is empty.

title: Wrote a grammar skill with American conventions and American sources; the person wanted British English and British academic references
trigger: Any task that produces prose, or rules about prose, for this person: documentation, skills, commit messages, replies, style guides. Signal: the person writes British spellings (for example "licence") and asks for "proper English". Nobody has said which variety, so the default is chosen silently.
prevention: Write every piece of prose and every language rule for this person in British English (-ise/-yse, -our, -re, single quotation marks, day-month-year dates), and cite British academic or publisher sources (the Oxford English Dictionary, Oxford and Cambridge University Press works, university and learned-society style guides) instead of American ones, unless the person asks for another variety.
detection: `grep -rniE "[a-z]+(ize|izing|ization|yze)\b|\bcolor|behavior|\bcenter\b|\bdefense\b" <changed prose files>` finds only quotations, identifiers and proper names; the reference list of any style or grammar document contains no purdue.edu, merriam-webster.com or chicagomanualofstyle.org entries.

title: Several plan and pre-mortem controls were never delivered and were not listed as deviations
trigger: Closing implementation of a plan whose steps and pre-mortem controls were written before the code.
prevention: Before closing implementation, map every plan step and pre-mortem control to a file or test that delivers it, and list each unmapped one in DEVIATIONS.md.
detection: Check that DEVIATIONS.md has a section naming each unmapped control; ls .github/workflows and grep -rni warn consonance show whether the CI and warning controls exist.

title: Stated unmeasured figures and untested causes as fact: a 'very likely exact' cause, an 'unchanged' anchor, a ~20 ms latency in a code comment, a README behaviour
trigger: Writing an explanation, a summary of a change, a number in a code comment, or a behaviour claim in documentation.
prevention: Every number, causal claim, or behaviour claim written into code, docs, or a reply must cite the measurement, test, or code location that supports it in the same turn, or carry the word UNVERIFIED.
detection: grep the diff for figures with units (ms, dB, Hz, %) and for 'because'/'likely'; each has a test, log line, K- item, or code reference beside it.

title: Do not interpolate credentials into shell command lines
trigger: Wanting to inspect token scopes or call an authenticated HTTP API from the shell while a token is held by `gh` or an env var.
prevention: Never expand a credential into a command line, URL, header argument or file; use the tool's own authenticated client.
detection: `grep -nE 'auth token|Bearer \$|github_pat_' <session commands / scripts>` finds nothing.

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum was adopted after the work was done, so no existing lessons were loaded before planning or implementing
trigger: A protocol addendum is given to follow after the implementation. Signal: the run has no loaded-lessons list, no gate record, no checkpoint fields.
prevention: Load lessons whose domain: or tech: tags match the task before planning, even without a protocol requirement; the store README states the matching rule.
detection: The first message of a run lists the loaded lesson ids.

title: Checkpoint state was back-filled, and no execution or deviation log was kept
trigger: A long run is resumed after a context reset and its progress is reconstructed from the final state of the files.
prevention: Write the checkpoint file at the time of each checkpoint from what exists at that moment, and append to a log as each step finishes. After a reset, add a dated note rather than rewriting earlier entries.
detection: Run: git show <checkpoint-commit>:.checkpoints/state.json ; every listed artefact must exist in that commit (git ls-tree).

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum was attached after planning and implementation had finished
trigger: The user supplies the lessons and knowledge addendum in a later message than the protocol.
prevention: At intake, ask whether the lessons and knowledge repositories exist and attach them before any research, even if the addendum has not been supplied.
detection: Check: the run log has a Before-run entry listing lessons loaded, dated before the first research commit.

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum was adopted after planning and implementation, so Before-run (R0) never happened
trigger: A protocol addendum is supplied after the work. Signal: the first mention of the lessons store is at the end.
prevention: Load relevant lessons at intake of every task and note which were loaded in the intake file.
detection: Intake file has a 'lessons loaded' line; empty is flagged.

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum arrived after planning and implementation, so no store was consulted and nothing was recorded in-run
trigger: A run starts without a knowledge store location in the intake, and the user supplies the addendum afterwards.
prevention: At Phase 0, if the knowledge store is not named in intake, ask for it once, and until it is named load the default store (a repository called Lessons or knowledge owned by the target repo's owner) before research starts.
detection: `.checkpoints/state.json` has `knowledge_store.commit_read` set before the first research commit.

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum arrived after planning, implementation and a research spin-off, so nothing was loaded or recorded during the run
trigger: A task starts without the addendum in hand and without the person naming a lessons or knowledge store, although `qualitycoding/Lessons` and `qualitycoding/knowledge` exist and can be read anonymously.
prevention: On the first turn of any task, before research, run `git ls-remote https://github.com/qualitycoding/Lessons HEAD` and the same for `knowledge`; if both answer, load the lessons whose tags match the task and tell the person which tags were used, whether or not the addendum was supplied.
detection: The first reply of the task names the store commits read, or says that the stores could not be read.

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum arrived after planning and nearly all of implementation, so R0 was skipped and corrections were not recorded as they happened
trigger: A long run under protocol v3.1 with no lessons store named at intake, although qualitycoding/Lessons and qualitycoding/knowledge exist.
prevention: On the first turn of any task, before research, clone or ls-remote qualitycoding/Lessons and qualitycoding/knowledge (anonymously or with the session credentials), load the lessons whose tags match the task, and tell the human which tags and commits were used, whether or not the addendum was supplied.
detection: The first reply of the task names the store commits read, or says that the stores could not be read.

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum arrived after planning and implementation, so the stores were not read before research
trigger: A long run under planning protocol v3.1 where the user's Lessons and knowledge repositories exist but the task does not name them.
prevention: Add a first plan step S-000 that clones qualitycoding/Lessons and qualitycoding/knowledge, lists the lessons matching the task's tags and records the commits read, and do not start research until it is done.
detection: plan/PLAN.md starts with S-000, and .checkpoints/state.json holds knowledge_store.commit_read.

title: The lessons and knowledge addendum arrived after planning and implementation, so no stored lesson was loaded for the VCV port
trigger: A long run under planning protocol v3.1 where the Lessons and knowledge repositories exist but the task does not name them.
prevention: Make S-000 the first plan step: clone qualitycoding/Lessons and qualitycoding/knowledge, list the lessons matching the task's tags, record the commits read in state.json, and start no research until it is done.
detection: plan/PLAN.md starts with S-000 and .checkpoints/state.json holds knowledge_store.commit_read.

title: The R0 application table quoted the triage proposals, not the plan text that was adopted
trigger: Prior-knowledge triage is delegated to agents that return, per lesson, a proposed amendment, and a generator renders those proposals into the record the implementer reads (`research/PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE.md`), while the planner later edits the plan with different wording, paths or strength.
prevention: After applying triage proposals, render the record from where each was applied (file and section), not from the proposal; label any proposal that was not adopted in full as "partly applied" with the reason, and grep the record for paths that do not exist in the plan.
detection: Every path named in an "applied"/"amended" row of `research/PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE.md` appears in `plan/` or `HANDOFF.md` (`grep -oE '`[a-z_./-]+/[a-z_./-]+`'` and look each up).

title: Knowledge store location taken from protocol default instead of verified with the human
trigger: Intake asks for a knowledge store (Rule 13) and the human has not named one explicitly. Temptation: adopt the protocol's default proposal (`agent-knowledge`) without flagging it as a guess needing confirmation.
prevention: When the intake batch includes a knowledge store, always present the proposed location explicitly as its own numbered intake item and probe its existence (`git ls-remote` / repo API) before recording it; never silently adopt the protocol default.
detection: `plan/ASSUMPTIONS.md` A-008 shows a probed location (access attempt result recorded) and matches what the human stated; `.checkpoints/state.json` `knowledge_store.location` equals the same value.

title: Rollout-phase addendum commits cause predictable source-tip drift — verify the parent chain before blocking
trigger: A cross-repository controller listed audited source commits, but the rollout phase had committed each addendum plan on top of the audited planning branch before the implementing agent started.
prevention: When a controller pins audited source commits but a rollout phase publishes artifacts onto the same branches, expect uniform one-commit drift and verify parentage instead of comparing SHAs; write the observed SHA and the parent-chain evidence into the per-repository deviation record.
detection: `git log --format='%H %P %s' -1 <source-branch>` shows exactly one parent matching the audited commit and an addendum-publication message.

title: Source facts were lost across a context reset and a note understated what had been checked
trigger: A long planning run is compacted into a summary and the research notes are written afterwards from that summary.
prevention: Write each source into the round log's 'Sources checked' section as it is opened, with its outcome and licence, so that a context reset cannot erase it.
detection: At every compaction point, compare the round log's source count with the number of fetch and search calls in the session record.

title: Amendment rounds left stale wording that contradicted the new decisions, and the consistency checker only counted IDs
trigger: Applying a batch of amendments to a plan made of several linked files (decisions, tests, steps, gates, register).
prevention: After every amendment batch, search the whole plan for the phrases the batch superseded and fix or mark each hit, and add those phrases to the mechanical checker so the next batch is covered automatically.
detection: A checker rule failing on any occurrence of a registered superseded phrase outside a line marked as superseded.

title: Tests were specified for owner-only controls that an agent holding the owner's credential can bypass
trigger: A plan whose gates, reviews or protections rely on a second identity, while the implementing agent runs under the owner's admin credential.
prevention: Before specifying a control, ask which identity can execute and which can approve it. If the same identity does both, record the control as procedural and the consequences as an accepted risk; do not write a test that presumes two identities.
detection: For each gate or protection in the plan, a line naming the approving identity and the executing identity; flag any where they are the same.

title: Audacity scripting commands and their semantics were coded from memory and shipped without checking the reference
trigger: Writing code that drives an external application or API which cannot be run in the sandbox (here: Audacity through mod-script-pipe), so command names, parameters and semantics come from recollection.
prevention: Strengthens L-20261004T102001Z: before shipping code that calls an external command set or API you cannot execute, fetch its official reference in the same turn, record each command used as a K- item with its locator, and mark any command you could not confirm as UNVERIFIED in a code comment and in the reply.
detection: For each command string sent by the integration code (grep the send/cmd calls), a K- item with a reference locator exists, or the call carries an UNVERIFIED comment.

title: An edit chained after a command that timed out never ran, and the omission was found only at the link step
trigger: A single shell line that does a slow step and then an edit with `&&`/`;`. Signal: the later error mentions something the edit should already have fixed.
prevention: Run each edit as its own call and confirm it with grep or a diff before starting the slow step.
detection: grep for the changed line appears in the log before the build starts.

title: Environment-class probe skipped at run start cost days of rebuilds on an ephemeral sandbox
trigger: A run starts implementation (S-000 onward) in an agent sandbox without recording whether the environment is stable or ephemeral. Signals: /tmp contents vanish between turns, binaries copied from the durable mount refuse to run, background jobs disappear, the compiler reads stale bytes.
prevention: Before the first build step of any run, classify the environment as stable or ephemeral with observed evidence and record it in the environment document; if ephemeral, put the restaging script and durable-surface layout in place before the first configure.
detection: `grep -q ephemeral plan/ENVIRONMENT.md` succeeds before the first cmake invocation; a run with builds but no environment-class record fails review.

title: Stage the complete CMake package when a mount cannot execute binaries
trigger: A Python-provided CMake binary is installed on a mount that forbids executable files, or only its `bin` directory is copied to executable local storage.
prevention: When restaging Python-provided CMake from a no-exec mount, copy the complete `cmake/data` tree, restore executable bits only in its `bin` directory, and invoke the staged binary directly rather than relying on a module entry point.
detection: Both staged binaries print their exact expected versions and exit zero without `CMAKE_ROOT` errors.

title: Codeberg was declared 'not on the allowlist' without checking; the configuration listed it but the live per-container proxy was stale
trigger: A push to a host the user says they allowed fails from the sandbox with a proxy denial.
prevention: When a host is reported unreachable, read `$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status` and the allowlist configuration before attributing the failure to either.
detection: The report quotes the proxy status output next to the claim about the allowlist.

title: A change spanning five files was sent as separate code snippets and only partly applied, leaving the string-count and A4-reference wiring half done
trigger: A change that touches more than three files (TuningEngine, PluginProcessor, MicrotonalVoice, the editor, CMake) delivered as prose with snippets, with the resulting files never returned for review.
prevention: After a multi-file change is sent as snippets, ask for the files or read the repository and grep for each new write (here `currentNumStrings.store`) before building the next feature on it; prefer returning whole files over snippets.
detection: `grep -n 'currentNumStrings.store' PluginProcessor.cpp` is non-empty and `grep -n 'referenceFrequency' TuningEngine.cpp` shows a read.

title: The C++ header generator emitted float literals such as `100f` and subnormal constants, which failed to compile or silently flushed to zero
trigger: A script that writes numeric constants into C++ source. Signal: a compile error on a literal like `100f`, or a constant that reads as 0 at runtime.
prevention: A code generator must format every number through one function that guarantees a valid literal for the target type, and tests the result by compiling it.
detection: CI compiles the generated header and a test reads back three sample constants, one whole-number and one tiny.

title: Draft test T-021 could not pass: it fed zero volts before the Schmitt trigger's UNINITIALIZED check
trigger: Writing tests for a trigger input that uses rack::dsp::SchmittTrigger, whose first process() call leaves the UNINITIALIZED state without firing.
prevention: Before freezing any test, run it against an independent oracle implementation of the decision and fix every test the oracle cannot pass.
detection: research/spikes/kitcore_oracle/oracle_run.txt lists every frozen test as PASS before the freeze commit.

title: Mull re-runs the whole test executable once per mutant, so a 12-minute suite makes mutation testing infeasible without a subset
trigger: Adding Mull to a project whose test executable takes minutes to run, or whose baseline run times out at Mull's default.
prevention: Time the unit executable before wiring up Mull; budget mutants x suite time / workers against the job limit, and choose the test subset up front.
detection: The Mull log's `Warm up run ... Finished in` line is below a minute or two.

title: Assumed the working tree persisted across turns; the sandbox had been reset
trigger: A later turn continues a run and the first command is cd into a directory created in an earlier turn.
prevention: At the start of each turn that continues a run, verify the working tree with git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD, restore from the remote if it fails, and refresh the exported bundle after every push.
detection: Run: git -C /home/claude/cons-plan rev-parse HEAD && git ls-remote origin ; then git bundle list-heads /mnt/user-data/outputs/consonance-repo.bundle ; heads must match the pushed ones.

title: git push failed with a server-side unpack error reproducibly, regardless of branch, content, or credential; the GitHub REST Git Data API succeeded immediately
trigger: git push (smart-HTTP) to a GitHub repository fails with a server-side "did not receive expected object <hash>" / "remote unpack failed: index-pack failed" error.
prevention: If git push fails with a server-side unpack/index-pack error that persists across retries with different refs, content, and credentials, stop retrying the pack-transport path (it is very likely a sandbox/proxy transport issue, not a repository or permissions problem) and fall back to the GitHub REST Git Data API for the push.
detection: A minimal test push (a few KB, unrelated content) succeeding while the real push fails identically across >=2 varied retries is the signal to stop retrying git push and switch to the API.

title: Bulk-deleting a directory to remove stray untracked files also removed a file that was actually tracked and committed
trigger: Cleaning up unexpected or stray-looking files/directories found in a git working tree, where the directory in question contains a mix of untracked stray content and legitimately tracked content.
prevention: Before bulk-deleting any directory in a git working tree to clean up stray files, run git status --short on that path first and delete only what shows as untracked (??); never rm -rf a directory that might contain tracked content without checking first.
detection: git status --short <path> before any rm -rf <path>; if any line does not start with '??', stop and delete file-by-file instead.

title: Continuing work from the local branch after an API-based push left local history diverged from what was actually on GitHub
trigger: A push was made via the GitHub REST API (blob/tree/commit/ref) rather than git push, and a later turn continues work by cd-ing into the same local clone and committing on top of its existing local HEAD.
prevention: After any push performed via a non-git-push mechanism (the GitHub API, a bundle import, etc.), treat the local branch as stale: fetch and reset to the remote tip before making further commits, rather than continuing to build on the pre-push local HEAD.
detection: git fetch <remote> && git diff --stat <local-HEAD> <remote>/main; a non-empty, non-cosmetic diff (or a diverged, non-fast-forward graph) means the local branch must be reset before continuing.

title: A shell loop applying the same edit to two branches continued after git checkout failed, running the edits against the wrong branch
trigger: Applying an identical change to several branches from one script.
prevention: When editing several branches, commit or stash and confirm 'git branch --show-current' before each branch's edits, and run multi-branch scripts with 'set -e' so a failed checkout stops them.
detection: Each branch's commit is made directly after its own edits, and 'git status --short' is empty before every checkout.

title: The whole build directory, including the render tools and analysis scripts, vanished between turns; only the delivered files survived
trigger: The first command of a turn that continues a build: `ls <work dir>` shows the directory empty or gone. No git repository and no bundle of the work tree existed.
prevention: On the first turn of a build, `git init` the work directory and commit after each file group; copy an archive or bundle of the whole tree (tools and scripts included, not only deliverables) to /mnt/user-data/outputs after each milestone; at the start of every later turn, run `git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD` before anything else. Strengthens L-20261004T102007Z, whose rule was not followed.
detection: `git -C <work dir> rev-parse HEAD` succeeds at the start of the turn, and `ls /mnt/user-data/outputs` lists a bundle newer than the last edit.

title: Fixed the project from the files delivered in chat, then found the project repository's main had a different engine and could not take the fixes
trigger: A request to put fixes 'to the project repo' for a project that earlier turns delivered as a zip, when the user's notes name a GitHub repository for that project.
prevention: Before fixing a project that has a named repository, clone it first (or ask the user for the path) and compare its current state with the files being fixed; say in the first reply which of the two the fixes are for.
detection: The first command of a fix task on a named project is a clone or fetch of that repository plus `git log -1` and a diff against the working files; the reply names the commit.

title: Workflow files were pushed straight to main, which diverged history from the PR branch and conflicted the pull request
trigger: Putting files on the default branch outside the PR that carries the rest of the work. Signal: main has a commit that the feature branch does not.
prevention: When a file must exist on main early, commit the same final content in both places, or bootstrap a minimal workflow that the branch does not override; diff before choosing a merge strategy.
detection: After any merge with -X ours or -X theirs, diff the discarded side against the result and record the diff in the commit message.

title: The plan's per-step commits and deviation records were not kept: one implementation commit, no DEVIATIONS.md, claims.json, GATES.md
trigger: A multi-step plan that says 'each step commits on its own' and 'state.json is rewritten after every checkpoint'.
prevention: Commit once per plan step and rewrite .checkpoints/state.json in that commit; open DEVIATIONS.md at the first departure from the plan, and list in it every changed assertion, dropped test, or section-3.3 behaviour not built.
detection: `git log --oneline <plan-commit>..HEAD | wc -l` is at least the number of implemented steps, and DEVIATIONS.md exists whenever state.json has a non-empty test_harness_fixes.

title: Work continued on a local clone that was behind origin, so a merged pull request was found only on pulling, and the clone was later lost in a sandbox reset
trigger: A run continues over several turns while the owner also commits to the same repository, or the sandbox is reset between turns.
