prevention: At the start of each turn that continues a run, run `git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD` and `git fetch origin && git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main`; before numbering any spike, decision or test, list the existing IDs on origin.
detection: `git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main` prints nothing before a new commit, and the next free ID is chosen from `git ls-tree -r origin/main`.

title: Steps S-001 to S-007 were committed in one 66-file commit, with no DEVIATIONS.md and no execution log
trigger: An implementation of seven or more plan steps is done in a single working session without a commit, a checkpoint update and a deviation entry per step.
prevention: Commit once per plan step, rewrite `.checkpoints/state.json` in that commit, and open DEVIATIONS.md at the first departure from the plan with one line per changed assertion or decision.
detection: `git log --oneline` has one commit per completed step ID, and `.checkpoints/state.json` `completed_steps` grows by one entry in each.

title: A history rewrite with git filter-branch (author email change) was followed by a force push whose lease named the wrong remote head, which was rejected as stale
trigger: A commit author or email must change across published history.
prevention: Before a history rewrite, record the remote HEAD from `git ls-remote` and use it as the explicit lease; never fall back to --force.
detection: The push command contains --force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha> with the sha from ls-remote in the same step.

title: Proxy-injected GIT_CONFIG_* and GH_TOKEN variables break fetch with a valid token; token variable lost on environment reset
trigger: 'Invalid username or token' from git fetch with a token known to be valid; env shows GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN set by the sandbox.
prevention: Before diagnosing a git credential failure, print the names (never values) of GIT_*, GH_* and GITHUB_* variables and run the command with them unset and an explicit askpass helper; only then conclude the token is bad.
detection: env | grep -E '^(GIT_CONFIG|GH_TOKEN|GITHUB_TOKEN)' | cut -d= -f1 was run before any 'token invalid' conclusion.

title: Upload zip built with an exclude-dotfiles pattern silently omitted .checkpoints/
trigger: Building a zip of changed files for manual upload with 'zip -x' patterns such as '.*'; the repo has required dot-directories (.checkpoints/).
prevention: Before sending any upload bundle, compare 'unzip -l <zip>' to 'git diff --name-status <remote-tip>..HEAD' and require an exact match, including dot-directories.
detection: diff <(unzip -Z1 bundle.zip | sort) <(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM remote..HEAD | sort) prints nothing.

title: Deviation records cited spikes in /tmp that were never committed and did not survive into the next session
trigger: A deviation or claim rests on a throwaway probe written to /tmp or a scratch copy of the firmware. Signal: the record says 'spike: /tmp ...'.
prevention: Commit every spike that backs a deviation or a claim to research/spikes/<name>/ together with its output before citing it, and never cite a path under /tmp.
detection: grep -rn '/tmp' DEVIATIONS.md evidence plan research returns nothing.

title: The pasted access token stayed in .git/config as part of the origin URL after the insteadOf entry was unset
trigger: A personal access token pasted in chat is used for git, and the repository is later published, zipped or inspected.
prevention: After any push that used a pasted token, run `git config --get-regexp 'url|remote'` and grep the repository for `github_pat_` and `ghp_`, and clean what you find before the turn ends.
detection: `grep -rIl 'github_pat_\|ghp_' .git/config . ` prints nothing.

title: A byte-hash manifest failed on Windows because git checked the files out with CRLF
trigger: `sha256sum -c MANIFEST` passes on Linux and fails on the `windows-latest` runner with "No such file or directory" for a name ending in `\r`, or a hash mismatch.
prevention: Whenever a repository stores hashes of file bytes, ship a `.gitattributes` that pins those paths to LF, and run the verification on Windows in CI.
detection: `sha256sum -c` is part of the Windows job and passes.

title: The /mnt/agents portal mount forbids symlinks and exec bits — stage node/git work in /tmp
trigger: Running `npm ci` or git index operations with the repo on the durable fuse portal mount (`/mnt/agents`).
prevention: Treat only the mount as durable, never as a build surface: stage builds in /tmp, copy artifacts back, retry lock-file operations, chmod after every copy from the mount.
detection: Build/test commands reference /tmp paths in the session log; deliverable diffs live on the mount.

title: A bootstrap that resets the implementation branch can discard unpushed work
trigger: A self-initialising script re-runs after an interruption in a working copy that already holds local commits on the implementation branch.
prevention: A bootstrap or resume script must never reset, force-checkout or delete a branch; it fast-forwards or stops with a distinct exit code.
detection: Run the script three times in one directory, with a local-only commit made between runs; the commit must still be there and the exit code 0 or 6.

title: Detached retry loops must live on durable storage
The deploy workflow broke on an empty ref input and its deploy job checked out main instead of the tag
trigger: A workflow_dispatch input used as a checkout ref in two jobs. Signal: the first dispatch from the UI, with the field left blank.
prevention: Dry-run the release workflow, including the rollback input, on a throwaway ref before the release gate, and give every input a non-empty default.
detection: OPERATIONS.md rollback drill run once before G-002, not after.

title: The plan's mitigation for workflow_dispatch needing the default branch left the person unable to find the Actions button
trigger: Asking a person to run a workflow from the Actions tab while the workflow exists only on a feature branch. Signal: 'I can't find the actions'.
prevention: If a manual dispatch is on the critical path, put a minimal dispatchable workflow on the default branch in the bootstrap step and state the exact UI path to the person.
detection: Each human-run step in the plan lists where its trigger lives and on which branch.

title: The plan pinned pluginval 2.0.0 and the action tag v2, neither of which exists; CI failed before testing anything
trigger: A plan or workflow pins a tool or action version by name (`@v2`, "2.0.0") that was never looked up against the project's published tags and releases.
prevention: Resolve every pinned version against the upstream tag/release list (`gh api repos/<o>/<r>/releases`, `git ls-remote --tags`) when writing the plan, and check the defaults of any wrapper action that downloads a second artifact.
detection: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag>` returns 200 for every pin.

title: A previous conformance review marked items DONE that the tree did not fully satisfy; a second pass found swallowed failures, an ungated latency threshold and a wrong run id
trigger: A review document or hand-off says a protocol or checklist item is DONE or FIXED, and a later pass is asked to re-check against the same protocol.
prevention: Treat a "DONE" in a prior review as a hypothesis: for each item run the grep, read the exit path, or open the run, and record the evidence next to the verdict.
detection: Each verdict row in a conformance review cites a file:line, a command output or a run id that a reader can open.

title: GitHub Actions rules about GITHUB_TOKEN, workflow triggers and scheduled workflows invalidated several design choices
trigger: Designing an unattended GitHub Actions pipeline that commits state, publishes Pages and raises its own alarms.
prevention: When a design relies on one workflow causing another, on a bot pushing to a protected branch, or on a scheduled alarm, check GitHub's documented behaviour for GITHUB_TOKEN, workflow_run and the 60-day rule before fixing the design.
detection: A design review checklist item per pipeline: what triggers each workflow, which token pushes, what protects the target branch, and what runs if the schedule is disabled.

title: The token was removed after the first push, so the push of the implementation branch needed another token
trigger: A PAT was pasted in chat for a push, then scrubbed from the sandbox, and a later push was needed.
prevention: At the start of a run that will push more than once, use add_repo for the repositories. If a PAT must be used, tell the user at once that it will be needed again, and ask for revocation at the end.
detection: Run: git ls-remote origin before the final step ; and grep -r 'github_pat_' the working tree and .git/config (must be empty).

title: A token pasted in chat was needed three times in one run; each time it had to be verified, used and scrubbed
trigger: The user supplies a personal access token in a message, not in session configuration. Signal: pushes fail with 403 until the token is used.
prevention: Ask at intake whether the session has repository access with push rights, and plan all pushes together so the credential is used once.
detection: A push step checks `git remote -v` and the environment for the token and fails if either holds it afterwards.

title: A permission probe overwrote the body of PR #1
trigger: Testing what a token can do by sending a write request. Signal: the probe is a PATCH to a live object.
prevention: Probe scopes with read endpoints or a GET of /user, /repos and the permissions field, or on a throwaway object created for the purpose; never write to a live object to test.
detection: Before any write probe, read and keep the current value, and write it back in the same call chain.

title: A pasted GitHub token returned 401 and the remote branches r1-r3 were never pushed; add_repo was the working route
trigger: The user pastes a `github_pat_***` token and asks for the remote to be checked and updated.
prevention: When asked to push to a GitHub repo, call add_repo with access=push for it before trying any user-supplied token; if a token is pasted anyway, never write it to any file and treat it as exposed (advise revoking it).
detection: `git ls-remote origin` lists every branch named in the plan's branch history, and `grep -r 'github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]\{20,\}' .` finds nothing.

title: Pasted tokens failed in three different ways, and an unpushed commit survives only as a bundle
trigger: The person pastes a fine-grained personal access token in chat to push to a repository, repeatedly, and the repository is not attached to the session with push access.
prevention: At the start of any run that will push, call `add_repo` with access `push` for the target; if it returns read-only, tell the person at once that one token with Contents and Workflows write is needed, plan all pushes for a single use, and ask for revocation at the end.
detection: `git ls-remote origin` succeeds before the final step; `grep -r 'github_pat_' .` over the working tree and `.git/config` returns nothing.

title: Manual GitHub web upload went to the wrong branch, and upload instructions were ambiguous about overwrite versus new files
trigger: The human uploads zip contents through the GitHub web UI because push is unavailable.
prevention: Ship every upload bundle with an UPLOAD.md that states the target branch, each path, and whether it overwrites, adds or deletes, and verify afterwards by comparing tree hashes of the fetched tip with the expected tree.
detection: git rev-parse origin/<branch>^{tree} equals the tree of the local commit that was meant to be uploaded.

title: Lessons and knowledge repositories could not be read because they were not attached to the session
trigger: The task names a GitHub repository as a store or target, but gh api repos/<owner>/<repo> answers 'GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session'.
prevention: Strengthened (add_repo was not available this time): at intake (0.3.7), probe 'gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>' for every repository the task names; if access is not enabled, tell the human immediately which repositories to attach instead of discovering it at the closing step.
detection: state.json knowledge_store.readable is set from a real probe at intake, with the probe output recorded.

title: An add_repo call came back 'NOT RUN' and the turn ended with 'No response requested', leaving the user's request undone
trigger: The first tool call of a turn that attaches repositories returns 'NOT RUN' or no result.
prevention: If a tool result says NOT RUN, call the tool again before writing any closing text, and end a turn only when the user's request has an answer.
detection: No assistant turn ends with 'No response requested' while the last tool result begins with NOT RUN.

title: Bearer extraHeader did not authenticate Git smart HTTP
trigger: GitHub API bearer authentication succeeds but `git push` still requests a username when using only `http.extraHeader`.
prevention: Verify Git smart-HTTP access with a non-mutating push through an ephemeral credential helper before relying on repository write access.
detection: `git push --dry-run` exits 0 without writing a ref or printing a credential prompt.

title: Final push preflight must include remote and resumed-session authentication
trigger: A planning run resumes in a new execution context after earlier pushes used an ephemeral credential helper, and the final phase assumes the remote and authentication still exist.
prevention: Before the final planning commit, verify the target remote and run an authenticated `git ls-remote` with a non-secret ephemeral credential path; if either is unavailable, report the persistence limitation rather than claiming a push.
detection: `git remote get-url origin` names the target and an authenticated `git ls-remote origin` exits 0 before a push is claimed; after fallback, `git bundle verify <bundle-path>` succeeds and the bundle lists the final generation-branch commit.

title: Commit the GATE-<id>.md record in the same commit that applies the human's gate response
trigger: A human gate (G-003) response is applied (real-device figures committed to perf/results, README updated) but the gate's own evidence file is written to a branch state that never reaches main.
prevention: The commit that applies a gate response also adds/updates the gate record file on the branch that will merge; the merge checklist includes "GATE-*.md for every gate passed".
detection: `ls GATE-*.md` on main covers every G-### in plan/GATES.md (or records why absent).

title: Repository creation and the Pages settings API were refused by the session proxy and had to be requested from the owner mid-run
trigger: The task asks the agent to create a new GitHub repository and publish it with GitHub Pages from a Claude cloud session.
prevention: In the first reply of any task that needs a new repository or a hosting setting, probe the call (or assume it is refused in a Claude cloud session) and ask the owner for every such human action in one message, with the exact setting.
detection: The first agent message of the run lists every repository to create and every settings change the agent cannot make.

title: Git credential-cache rejected the durable mount's socket-directory permissions
trigger: Git credential-cache is configured with its socket on the sandbox's durable FUSE-style mount.
prevention: Place Git credential-cache sockets in a mode-0700 temporary directory, never in repository artifacts or on a mount whose permissions cannot be tightened.
detection: A redacted `git credential fill` returns a username and password without exposing the secret and without a daemon warning.

title: Credential helpers on the durable mount cannot be executed
trigger: A Git askpass or push helper is stored on `/mnt/agents` and invoked directly.
prevention: Stage every executable helper onto executable local storage and run a trivial invocation before using it for Git.
detection: The credential helper responds to a username prompt and `git ls-remote` succeeds without exposing the token.

title: Voice interface lacked accessors the plugin host layer needs
trigger: Freezing core headers (stubs) for a voice class that a JUCE AudioProcessor will wrap.
prevention: Before freezing interfaces, list every value the plugin layer must read from the core (latency, UI state snapshot, tuning, parameter ranges) and give each an accessor in the stub header.
detection: Every host-facing requirement in DECISIONS.md names the header method that provides it.

title: The editor's MIDI-note label array was typed separately and in a different order from the processor's note map: 14 of 15 labels are wrong, and three UI ranges differ from the engine's
trigger: The same numeric table (MIDI notes, parameter ranges, defaults) written in more than one file: a `switch` in the processor, a label array in the editor, a ParamSpec table, a README table.
prevention: Define every user-visible table (note numbers, labels, ranges, defaults) once in code and generate the editor, the parameter layout and the docs from it; where a second copy must exist, add a test that compares it with the source and fails on any difference. This strengthens L-20261004T150200Z, which covered a header versus a fixture only.
detection: A script that parses the editor's label array and the processor's `case N: return X;` lines reports 0 mismatches; `kParamSpecs` minimum and maximum equal `getRecipe(i).minHz` and `.maxHz` for all 15 instruments.

title: Attributed claims to sources that were not read or did not say it: a JUCE source comment 'pulled' from an empty fetch, a per-user VST3 folder 'per Steinberg's priority rules', 'JUCE never reads the channel', an invented reason, and an unconfirmed VST3_COPY_DIR option
trigger: Explaining a build error, a framework behaviour or a platform path in a reply, and wanting to sound grounded.
prevention: Do not write 'I read/pulled the source' unless a fetch in the same turn returned that text; give its URL, and mark every other claim about a framework or platform UNVERIFIED in the reply.
detection: Each sourced claim in a reply carries a URL that appears in a fetch or search result of the same turn.

title: Delivered about 600 lines of JUCE code (the neck component three times, processBlock routing, a mutex-guarded TuningEngine, the merged FretboardComponent) with no compile or syntax check and no 'not compiled' label
trigger: Writing JUCE C++ in a session where no JUCE tag has been fetched, and sending it as ready to paste.
prevention: Before sending JUCE code, syntax-check it against the pinned JUCE headers (`git clone --depth 1 --branch <tag>` of juce-framework/JUCE, then `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only` with the module include paths), or label every file NOT COMPILED in the reply and the README.
detection: The reply contains `compiled with <compiler> against JUCE <tag>` or `NOT COMPILED`.

title: The editor and tuning control compiled against real JUCE but were never run, and the planned smoke test was abandoned
trigger: UI work (PluginEditor.h/.cpp, EdoControl.h: layout, focus release, labels drawn inside dots, label culling) in a sandbox with no display and one CPU core, where a full JUCE module build takes longer than one 300 s tool call.
prevention: When UI code cannot be run, list every UI behaviour from the plan (PLAN section 3.3) in the checkpoint's `unverified` array, each mapped to an operational test ID, and move any decision that can be computed without a window (label culling, font fit, cache key) into a pure function with a unit test.
detection: `.checkpoints/state.json` has an `unverified` array whose length equals the number of section 3.3 bullets, and `grep -c 'shouldDrawFretLabel' tests/unit/*.cpp` is non-zero for each pure UI decision.

title: JUCE calls were written from memory: getCurrentTextEditor does not exist in 8.0.15, and the JUCE 8-only FontOptions has no version floor
trigger: Writing JUCE component code without the headers open, for a project whose CMakeLists adds JUCE from a hard-coded path (add_subdirectory("D:/JUCE")) with no version requirement.
prevention: Before using a JUCE API, grep the checked-out JUCE headers for it, and when a newer API is used add a minimum-version check (static_assert on JUCE_MAJOR_VERSION) to the project in the same commit.
detection: `grep -n 'JUCE_MAJOR_VERSION' *.h CMakeLists.txt` finds the check whenever FontOptions is used.

title: Just-intonation fret labels and cents are computed with 2^(fret/12) in the editor instead of from the engine's frequency
trigger: A plan says labels are computed from the frequency the engine will produce (PLAN section 3.1), and a UI cache needs a frequency per fret.
prevention: Compute every displayed pitch by calling the same engine function that produces the sound; add a test that, for each tuning mode, equates the label frequency to the engine frequency within 0.01 cent.
detection: `grep -n 'pow (2' PluginEditor.h PluginEditor.cpp` returns nothing.

title: The audio thread locks a mutex per call and the snapshot copies vectors; the pre-mortem only considered UI contention
trigger: A shared engine object read by both the message thread (painting) and the audio thread (note routing and voice start).
prevention: In every pre-mortem for an audio plugin, add a lens 'what does the audio thread lock, allocate, or wait on' and mitigate by lock-free reads of a preallocated snapshot.
detection: `grep -n 'lock_guard\|std::mutex' TuningEngine.*` shows no lock reachable from processBlock or renderNextBlock.

title: EdoControl differs from PLAN section 3.3 (no ParameterAttachment, mouse wheel, Escape or visible tooltip) and the deviation is not logged
trigger: A plan section lists UI behaviours (custom ParameterAttachment, mouse-wheel stepping, focus release on Enter, Escape and click-away, validation tooltip) and the implementation is judged by 'compiles'.
prevention: After implementing a UI section, tick each bullet of the plan section as built, deviated (with a DEVIATIONS.md entry) or not built; a bullet with no entry blocks the commit message from saying 'per plan'.
detection: A table in DEVIATIONS.md or the checkpoint has one row per bullet of PLAN section 3.3.

title: JUCE integration tests were frozen as 'compile-unverified (no JUCE in planning sandbox)' although JUCE 8.0.15 could be fetched and built later
trigger: A planning agent freezes tests that need a large dependency and records that the dependency is not available.
prevention: Before recording a dependency as unavailable in the planning sandbox, run the clone or install command and keep its error output in research/; if it works, compile the frozen tests against it before the freeze.
detection: research/ holds the failing command output whenever a frozen test is labelled compile-unverified.

title: Assumed JUCE's free tier requires GPL; JUCE 8 uses AGPLv3 plus a free closed-source Starter tier
trigger: Choosing a repo license for a JUCE project from memory ("JUCE is GPL or paid commercial") without reading the current EULA for the pinned major version.
prevention: For any framework with a paid tier, read the current EULA/licensing page for the pinned major version before writing the license assumption; never carry a licensing premise across major versions.
detection: `plan/ASSUMPTIONS.md` licensing item names the exact JUCE licence(s) of the pinned version (AGPLv3 / Starter / Indie / Pro for 8.x) and cites the EULA URL with an access date.

title: The Steinberg VST3 validator inside pluginval rejected an empty program name that the local suite could not see
trigger: A JUCE plugin whose `getNumPrograms()` is 1 or more and whose `getProgramName()` returns an empty string.
prevention: Run pluginval (strictness 5 or higher) in CI from the first build that produces a plugin binary; do not rely on unit tests for host-contract rules.
detection: pluginval's "vst3 validator" test passes on every OS in CI.

title: Review mutation survivors by lowest per-file score first: a 9% file hid a product bug
trigger: A first mutation run scores well under the floor and the report lists dozens of survivors.
prevention: Treat a file with a very low mutation score as "this stage may be untested or broken", and write a test from the stage's documentation before reading its mutants one by one.
detection: The per-file table is in the review document and no file under 50% lacks a stated reason.

title: Sandbox recycled mid-build; JUCE checkout and build tree lived only in /tmp
trigger: A long JUCE build exceeded the sandbox lifetime; the sandbox was recycled mid-build and `/tmp` (build dir, staged JUCE clone) was wiped. The next tool call returned `no sandboxes found with the provided IDs`.
prevention: Caches of expensive third-party checkouts live on the durable mount (`/mnt/agents/<name>-cache`), never only in `/tmp`; after any recycle, re-run the restage check before building.
detection: Before a long build, confirm the cache path exists on the mount (`test -d /mnt/agents/juce-cache/modules`); after a recycle, re-clone if missing.

title: JUCE 9 naive unity build incomplete; FUSE mount cannot hold build outputs
trigger: Building the JUCE 9 integration harness took six sandbox recycles; each retry taught something new about why a naive unity build was incomplete.
prevention: Never assume the primary unity file is the whole module; check for split units, headless cores, and amalgamated C units before first compile.
detection: After linking, `nm` the module objects for a known symbol (e.g. `Label::setText` must be defined, not U, in gui_basics).

title: An intermittent pluginval failure was only diagnosable once a host-style automation stress test reproduced it in CI
trigger: pluginval fails with "An unhandled exception was thrown!" in its Automation test on some runs and passes on others, after a change that moves work between threads.
prevention: For any change that touches threading or the audio path, add or run a host-style stress test (random parameter automation at several block sizes, re-prepare mid-run) in CI before merging; treat an intermittent pluginval failure as a reproducible bug to be captured by such a test, not as a flake.
detection: `automation_stress` passes in the sanitizer job on the branch before and after the change.

title: The editable install ran before pyproject.toml existed, and the pinned setuptools was flagged by pip-audit
trigger: A hash-locked environment is built before the project metadata and before an audit.
prevention: Create pyproject.toml, list the build backend in the input file, run pip-audit and a clean-room install in one step before any code is written.
detection: Run: pip-audit -r requirements.lock ; python -m venv /tmp/x && /tmp/x/bin/pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock && /tmp/x/bin/pip install -e .

title: The hash-locked environment omitted the build backend, and the first pin chosen for it was vulnerable
trigger: Building a --require-hashes lockfile and then installing the project itself editable. Signal: `Cannot import setuptools.build_meta`.
prevention: Include the build backend in the lock inputs from the start, and run pip-audit on the final lock before treating the environment as done.
detection: Clean-room install script runs `pip install --require-hashes` then `pip install -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation` and then pip-audit; the plan gate fails on any step.

title: Zoom cost was measured with inter-rAF deltas, which headless Chromium's simulated vsync masked at about 16.7 ms
trigger: A render-cost benchmark built on requestAnimationFrame timestamps in a headless browser. Signal: every frame reports the same value near 16.7 ms.
prevention: Time the work itself (performance.now around the call) for cost budgets; use frame deltas only for dropped-frame detection, and check the metric can take values other than its pacing floor.
detection: A harness self-test that injects a known 30 ms busy loop and asserts the reported figure rises.

title: Browser tests could not run in the sandbox, so four defects in the first implementation surfaced only after CI
trigger: A plan that already records 'e2e cannot run here' (R-003) and an implementation step reported complete on unit tests and a build. Signal: the risk is known and the mitigation is deferred to CI.
prevention: When the sandbox cannot run browsers, push a branch and trigger CI after the first UI step rather than after the last, and report 'implemented, unverified' per test until CI is green.
detection: A step is not marked done until the CI job for its tests has a run id recorded.

title: The browser test suite first ran one day after the whole implementation was pushed, because the sandbox could not run browsers
trigger: The sandbox cannot download Playwright browsers or reach the model host, so only Node unit tests can run during implementation, while the plan's critical tests are browser tests.
prevention: After the first step that adds a browser test, push the branch and run the CI browser job; until a CI run id is recorded in .checkpoints/state.json, list every browser test as 'implemented, unverified' in the handoff.
detection: `.checkpoints/state.json` has a CI run id for every step that added browser tests, dated before the next step starts.

title: First performance test dictated an unattainable budget instead of deriving it from the requirement
trigger: Writing a frozen performance-budget test before any implementation or measurement exists.
prevention: Derive every performance budget from a measured reference run or a stated requirement, and time only the public API that is meant to serve that workload.
detection: Run: grep -B3 'mark.perf' tests/*.py ; each perf test should have an adjacent comment naming the measured baseline or the requirement.

title: Reported test counts and freeze status were wrong or stale in the report, README, state file and a reply
trigger: Writing a report or reply that states how many tests exist or which are frozen.
prevention: Produce every test count in a report or reply from pytest --collect-only -q per file in the same turn, and never carry counts over from earlier text.
detection: Run: python -m pytest --collect-only -q -p no:cacheprovider | grep '::' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c ; compare with each count stated in README.md, IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md and .checkpoints/state.json.

title: Frozen test T-036 had a single-seed gauge search with a silent default and an unstated connectedness assumption
trigger: A test contains its own search or propagation algorithm (gauge fixing, graph traversal) with a fallback such as S[S==0]=1.
prevention: Test helpers that contain an algorithm must state their precondition, avoid silent defaults (assert the fallback path is never taken), and be tested on a hand-checkable synthetic case before the test is frozen.
detection: grep -n 'S\[S==0\]' tests/ returns nothing; each helper function in tests/ has a self-test.

title: First checkpoint save would have rotated a corrupt file over the only good backup
trigger: Writing a save routine that keeps a rolling backup (current -> .bak, then write new current).
prevention: In any rotate-to-backup routine, validate the file being rotated, never replace a backup with an unvalidated file, and test a save that follows a corrupted current file.
detection: Run: grep -n 'def test_.*corrupt' tests/*.py ; one test must save, corrupt the current file, save again, and assert the backup still loads. The frozen suite has no such test.

title: Two overlapping pitch-mode modules and test files were shipped; one is dead code
trigger: Adding a module for a capability (here the standard/free pitch switch) in a package that may already contain one.
prevention: Before adding a module, grep the package for one with the same responsibility and extend it; if two exist, name the unused one in DEVIATIONS.md before the push.
detection: Run: for m in consonance/*.py; do b=$(basename $m .py); [ $b = __init__ ] && continue; grep -rlw $b --include=*.py consonance scripts examples | grep -v "consonance/$b.py" >/dev/null || echo "unused: $m"; done

title: A Python str.replace()-based file edit reported success but made no change, because the search pattern did not match
trigger: Editing a file via a scripted, non-interactive search-and-replace (Python's str.replace, or equivalent) run inside a bash tool call, where the script prints a success message unconditionally.
prevention: After any non-interactive search-and-replace edit, immediately diff or grep the target file to confirm the expected change landed, rather than trusting a script's own completion message; prefer a replace primitive that fails loudly on a non-match over one (like Python's str.replace) that silently returns the input unchanged.
detection: git diff --stat <path> after the edit must show the file as changed; a str.replace()-based script with no post-edit diff/grep check is itself the anti-pattern to flag in review.

title: An index-generator script crashed partway through, and its root cause was fixed without re-running it to confirm the generated file was actually regenerated
trigger: A generated index/summary file is rebuilt by a script that processes several source files in a loop and writes its output only at the end (or only for a given section) once the loop completes without raising.
prevention: After fixing the root cause of a script crash, re-run that exact script to completion (not just a different validator) before committing its output, and verify any generated/derived file's basic invariant (e.g. entry count matches source file count) against a fresh clone, not the local working copy, before considering a push complete.
detection: `git clone` the just-pushed repository fresh into a new directory and recompute the invariant (e.g. `find knowledge -name 'K-*.md' | wc -l` vs the INDEX.md's own "Entries:" line) there, not in the working copy that produced the push.

title: Claude Code cloud sandbox has no pip, no ensurepip, no sudo and no cmake
trigger: Planning or implementing in a Claude Code cloud container (Ubuntu 24.04, user `claude`). Signals: `cmake: command not found`, `python3 -m venv` fails with "Failing command: .../venv/bin/python3", `No module named pip`, `sudo: a password is required`.
prevention: In a sandbox without sudo, create Python venvs with `--without-pip` plus get-pip.py and take build tools from release binaries; never assume apt or system pip.
detection: `<venv>/bin/pip --version` and `cmake --version` succeed before any spike runs; `plan/ENVIRONMENT.md` lists the no-sudo commands.

title: The CLI opened a transcript log file and only closed the transport in its finally block
trigger: A command-line tool opens a second resource (a log file) inside a factory function, away from the try/finally that cleans up the first resource.
prevention: Every resource opened by a tool must be released in the same finally block, or owned by a context manager. Add a test that the log file is closed (or flushed) after both a normal run and a run that raises.
detection: Run: grep -n 'TranscriptLog\|open(' src/tracer_diag/cli.py ; each hit must be inside a with statement or have a matching close() in a finally block.

title: Session code took element [0] of an adapter reply without checking that a line came back
trigger: Code sends an AT command and uses the first reply line directly.
prevention: When a reply from hardware is indexed, define what an empty reply means (an error type or a default) and test it. Make the fake adapter able to return an empty list for any command.
detection: Run: grep -n '\]\[0\]\|)\[0\]' src/tracer_diag/*.py ; each hit must have a length check or a test with an empty reply.

title: Solver studies exceeded the 4 to 5 minute tool limit; background runs were killed between calls and across container restarts
trigger: A sparse direct solve costs minutes per sweep on one core and a study needs hours.
prevention: Make every long study resumable from saved state and run it in slices shorter than the tool limit; test survival with a heartbeat before relying on a background process.
detection: The driver script accepts --slice and writes state after each slice.

title: Memory-heavy computations launched concurrently and without a memory pre-flight
trigger: Sparse eigen-solves or projector constructions with N above about 8e3 states, or two heavy jobs running at once, in a cgroup-limited container.
prevention: Before any job above N=5e3, estimate peak memory from nnz and compare with 'free -m' and the cgroup limit, abort if the estimate exceeds 60 percent, and never run two heavy jobs concurrently.
detection: logs show a pre-flight memory estimate line before each heavy run; dmesg has no OOM kills for the run.

title: src/ changes after the production run were not checked against D-025 until later
trigger: Any edit under src/ after results/*.json were produced (S-009), including 'schema' or 'densification' bug fixes.
prevention: Install a check (pre-commit or Makefile target) that fails when src/ changes while results/*.json carry an older provenance.git_commit, and run it at every step after S-009.
detection: make check-provenance exits 0 at each post-S-009 step.

title: Reassigned WaveShaperNode.curve on every drive change, which the spec forbids; a strict runtime threw InvalidStateError
trigger: Code changes the distortion amount of an existing WaveShaperNode by assigning a new Float32Array to .curve. Browsers tolerate it, so it works in manual testing.
prevention: Never assign WaveShaperNode.curve twice; to change a curve, build a new WaveShaperNode and swap it into the graph.
detection: grep shows no '.curve =' outside node construction, and a test calls setDrive repeatedly on node-web-audio-api without throwing (T-13b).

title: Treated DynamicsCompressorNode as a zero-latency brickwall limiter: it overshot the ceiling and delayed the paths it sat on
trigger: Adding DynamicsCompressorNode for limiting, or for glue on one bus of a parallel mix.
prevention: Do not use a DynamicsCompressorNode as a peak ceiling or place one on a subset of parallel paths; follow it with a clipper for a ceiling, and measure path latency with an impulse whenever a compressor is added.
detection: T-11 (true peak <= -1 dBFS) and T-26 (path latency spread <= 5 ms) pass.

title: Repeated the WaveShaper curve-reassignment mistake: the drive sliders assign .curve a second time on a node that already has one
trigger: A drive slider that changes the distortion amount of an existing WaveShaperNode. Signal: `.curve =` appears both at node construction and in a slider handler.
prevention: Before delivering Web Audio code, run `grep -n "\.curve *="`: every match must sit on a WaveShaperNode created in the same function; a drive change builds a new node (quantised) and swaps it in.
detection: `grep -n "\.curve *=" <file>` lists only lines inside node-construction helpers; a test calls the drive handler repeatedly on node-web-audio-api without throwing.

title: Repeated the compressor-as-ceiling mistake: the master bus ends in a DynamicsCompressorNode with no clipper and the peak was never measured
trigger: A master bus of several distorted, summed sources ending in a DynamicsCompressorNode. Signal: no WaveShaper or limiter after it.
prevention: A master chain that ends in a DynamicsCompressorNode must be followed by a clipper, and an offline render must show a true peak at or below -1 dBFS before the app is delivered.
detection: Render 60 s offline and print the maximum absolute sample; it is at most 0.89 (-1 dBFS), and `grep -n "createDynamicsCompressor" <file>` is followed by a WaveShaper in the graph.

title: Fitted the cabinet response only up to 4.6 kHz before measuring where the reference recording's energy lies (centroid about 4.8 kHz)
trigger: Fitting a filter or model to a reference recording over a chosen frequency range.
prevention: Measure the reference's spectral centroid and band-energy distribution before choosing a fitting range, and fit at least up to the frequency below which about 95% of its energy lies.
detection: The fit script prints the reference's energy distribution next to the chosen range.

title: The generated plate mode table fell short of the 160 modes the plan required because the eigenvalue search stopped at too low a lambda
trigger: Generating a table of N eigenfrequencies by scanning roots up to a fixed bound. Signal: fewer than N rows.
prevention: Choose the search bound from the required count (Weyl estimate N ~ lambda^2/4) with margin, and assert the row count after generation.
detection: The generator asserts len(table) >= required and exits non-zero otherwise.

title: A name-leak scan must skip raw audio sample bytes
trigger: A bundle verifier searches every file for reference stem names such as r05.
prevention: Scan metadata and file names; never raw sample bytes.
detection: Run the verifier on a bundle with random audio and short stem names.

title: Give the round cap an owner-controlled extension route and record it
trigger: A tool refuses a fourth round because the plan froze a three-round cap.
prevention: When freezing a cap on rounds, freeze the extension route with it and require each use to be recorded.
detection: Try to build round cap+1 with and without the extension variable.

title: A patch was assumed to have taken effect; the mushy-width default was 0.02, not 0.04, and studies were built on the wrong value
trigger: A multi-line edit changes a default parameter and a study is launched straight away.
prevention: Print the effective parameter values at the start of every study run and compare them with the intended values before the run proceeds.
detection: Each run log begins with a parameter dump.

title: Calibration targets were chosen before measuring the attainable score range
trigger: Choosing target values for a generator whose score has an unknown reachable range for the chosen sonority size.
prevention: Estimate the attainable score range for each sonority size by random search before choosing calibration targets, and print that range beside the targets.
detection: Run: grep -n 'Attainable' docs/CALIBRATION.md ; the table must be present and every target should sit inside it or be flagged.

title: A UI parameter's range was set to a model's full regression range instead of what the actual configuration can attain
trigger: Choosing the min/max range for a user-facing control (a target value fed to a directed sampler) from a model's published or fitted range, without first checking what the sampler's actual configuration (sonority size, window, candidate set) can reach.
prevention: Before setting a user-facing range for any target fed to a directed/weighted sampler, check the knowledge store (or run a quick attainable-range measurement) for the specific configuration being used, not the model's nominal or published range; this is now the second occurrence of this exact mistake in this codebase's history -- treat 'range = model's published range' as a default to actively distrust, not a safe shortcut.
detection: Any UI/parameter range table entry sourced from a model's 'published' or 'fitted' range, without a cited attainable-range measurement for the actual configuration in use, should be treated as unverified.

title: On "Restart", do not read earlier sessions' scratch state
trigger: The human says "Restart" (or rejects a resume attempt) while older session scratchpads or branches exist.
prevention: When told to restart, use only the remote repository and the current conversation as inputs; do not open other sessions' scratchpads.
detection: No command in the session references another session's scratchpad path after the restart message.

title: The addendum's gate ID G-003 collided with the plan's own G-003
trigger: Adding a protocol's fixed IDs to a project that already numbers its own gates. Signal: the same ID with two meanings.
prevention: Namespace gate IDs by source (for example PUSH-1) or allocate the next free number.
detection: ID checker covers gates and fails on a duplicate.

title: The checkpoint state was never updated after planning, and the implementation has no execution log
trigger: A run resumed in a later session that has a checkpoint file. Signal: state.json still shows phase 5.3 with '5.3 push' pending after the release.
prevention: Update state.json at the end of every implementation step and append to an execution log with step, commit, time and run id.
detection: A check that the last commit time and state.json 'phase' agree.

title: Probe the knowledge store's existence and name at intake; never adopt protocol defaults silently
trigger: A run starts under a protocol version whose knowledge-store default was later corrected (`agent-knowledge` → `knowledge`, planning-protocol-review corrections 2026-10-27), or — as here — predates the store entirely (plan of 2026-09-26 vs store introduced 2026-10-04).
prevention: At intake, verify the knowledge store is reachable and record its location + commit + readability in .checkpoints/state.json; if it postdates the work or is unreadable, record that in research/PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE.md — never assume the default silently.
detection: state.json `knowledge_store` field is non-empty on every run; PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE.md exists for runs claiming R0.

title: Output restrictions were set on a privacy assumption before asking what was already public
trigger: Designing log, artefact and output controls for a project whose data may already be public.
prevention: Ask the owner early which data is already public, and verify what can be verified (repository visibility through the API), before choosing what outputs must hide.
detection: An intake question listing each data set and its visibility, answered before the privacy design.

title: Gave Visual Studio 2022 commands (generator 'Visual Studio 17 2022', 'Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2022') although the build log named Visual Studio 18 and MSVC 19.50
trigger: Advising on a Windows C++ build when the person's own log shows the compiler path and version.
prevention: Read the compiler path and version from the person's log before naming a Visual Studio version or generator, and ask for the output of `cmake --help` (generator list) when a generator name is needed.
detection: The reply quotes the Visual Studio version found in the log.

title: ASan and full JUCE rebuilds exceeded the 300 s tool limit and background builds died between calls
trigger: A JUCE console-app build or an AddressSanitizer build on a single CPU core, started with `nohup` and `&` in one tool call and polled in the next.
prevention: For any build that may exceed 250 s, start it with `setsid nohup <cmd> > log 2>&1 < /dev/null &` and poll the log, or build one target per call with `timeout 280`; never start a long build without one of these two.
detection: The command line of every build call over 60 s contains either `setsid nohup ... < /dev/null` or `timeout 280`.

title: Work directories and the JUCE build tree vanished between turns and had to be recreated
trigger: A multi-turn session where compiled objects and checkouts live outside the committed repository.
prevention: Commit a script (tools/bootstrap_test_env.sh) that clones the pinned JUCE tag and configures the test targets, and run it as the first command of every turn that needs a build.
detection: tools/bootstrap_test_env.sh exists in the repository and its output is the first tool result of a build turn.

title: Status text still says 'compile-unverified' after the tests compiled, and retired test files keep FROZEN headers
trigger: A frozen-test table written at plan time is not revised after implementation, and superseded tests are moved rather than marked.
prevention: When a status changes, edit every row that states it; when a test is retired, replace its FROZEN header with 'RETIRED - not built' in the same commit and note it in FROZEN.md.
detection: `grep -rn 'FROZEN TEST SUITE' tests/retired` returns nothing and `grep -n 'Compile-unverified' tests/FROZEN.md` returns nothing after S4 passes.

title: The emulator's CLI batch mode does not print the pty path, so spike S1 had to read the port from the batch file
trigger: Driving a third-party simulator through its command line from a script. Signal: the process starts but the script has no handle to talk to it.
prevention: For a simulator you will drive from tests, check at the first spike that the in-process API exposes every handle you need, and prefer it over the CLI.
detection: The spike script asserts it received a device path within 5 seconds and fails loudly if not.

title: Ran `git add -A` before adding a .gitignore and committed the CMake and JUCE build trees, producing a 130 MB bundle
trigger: Making a commit or a bundle from a directory that also holds build output, with no .gitignore yet.
prevention: Create the .gitignore (build output directories) before the first `git add -A` in a directory where a build will run, and read `git status --short` before committing.
detection: `git diff --cached --stat | tail -1` before each commit shows no build directory; `ls -la` of any bundle or archive is checked against the expected size.

title: Wrote a new single-file Void Choir app from scratch although the user's notes list a Void Choir project repository that already has a tested engine
trigger: A request to write an app in a domain where the user's notes name a project repository for it. Signal: the memory index lists "Void Choir ... atmospheric black metal generator" with a GitHub repository.
prevention: When the user's notes list a project repository that matches the request's subject, clone it first and say in the first reply whether the work is for that repository or for a separate file.
detection: The first tool call of such a task is a clone or `git ls-remote` of the named repository, and the first reply names the commit.

title: `git add docs` staged a file from another task (docs/plan/00_REQUEST_AND_DIAGNOSIS.md) into the run's commit
trigger: Staging a whole directory in a repository that holds other people's or earlier work. Signal: `git status` lists files you did not write.
prevention: Stage by explicit file list and read `git diff --cached --stat` before every commit.
detection: The commit script prints the staged file list and compares it to the expected list.

title: A blanket `git add -A` committed emulator log files again
trigger: Committing right after running tests that write logs into the working tree. Signal: `elm.log` in `git status` as untracked.
prevention: Stage by explicit file list and read `git diff --cached --stat` before every commit; add .gitignore entries when a tool first writes a log.
detection: Commit helper prints the staged list and refuses anything matching *.log, build/ or dist/.

title: The .gitignore rule `*.onnx`, written to keep real models out of the repository, also excluded the tiny model fixtures the browser tests load
trigger: A .gitignore rule is written broadly (an extension) to keep large generated or downloaded files out, while small fixtures with the same extension are needed by tests.
prevention: After writing or editing .gitignore, run `git check-ignore -v` on every fixture path the tests read and `git status --short --ignored`; every needed file must print nothing from check-ignore.
detection: `git check-ignore -v tests/fixtures/*` prints nothing, and `git ls-files tests/fixtures` lists every fixture a test opens.

title: The .gitignore rule *.log left the logs that the manifest cites untracked; they were renamed to .txt
trigger: A manifest references result files by name and a .gitignore contains a broad extension pattern.
prevention: After writing or changing .gitignore, run `git ls-files` against every file the manifest names and fail on any missing one.
detection: A check script compares manifest file names with `git ls-files`.

title: The number of tracked files was typed into a verification prompt (29) when the repository had 30
trigger: A prompt or report states a count of files, commits or tests that was not computed at that moment.
prevention: Compute every count quoted in a report or prompt from the repository at that moment; never type one.
detection: Counts in released text are generated by a script.

title: The checkpoint state kept its planning-time phase and hash map through implementation, with 13 tracked files missing from it
trigger: Implementation steps are committed in groups and the checkpoint file is edited once at the end.
prevention: After each implementation step, regenerate the artifacts hash map and updated_at in .checkpoints/state.json from git ls-files and append one line to EXECUTION_LOG.md, with a make target so it is one command.
detection: python3 compare of the keys of state.json artifacts with git ls-files (excluding .checkpoints) prints nothing.

title: tools/trigsim/trigsim.elf and trigsim.hex were committed because a blanket git add -A ran with no .gitignore entry for that directory
trigger: A new tool directory is built in place and the step ends with git add -A.
prevention: Before a commit that adds a new directory, run git status --short and add files by name, or ignore the directory's build output first.
detection: git ls-files | grep -E '[.](elf|hex|o)$' prints nothing.

title: hardware/LICENSE was left as a pointer because the full CERN-OHL-P-2.0 text could not be obtained in the sandbox
trigger: A plan step creates licence files and the sandbox has no network route to the licence host. Signal: a curl to the licence URL fails.
prevention: At intake, list every licence file the plan needs and check that its full text is obtainable in the sandbox (/usr/share/common-licenses or an allowed host); if not, ask the owner for the text before S-001.
detection: Each LICENSE file in the repository is over 5 KB and starts with the licence's standard title.

title: state.json still said 5-complete after ten implementation steps, and the repository's default branch stayed on the planning branch
trigger: An implementation run writes its own checkpoint file next to the planner's, and publishes a new main branch.
prevention: At the last implementation step, update state.json (phase, steps done, tag) and run `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD`; the symref must name the branch you released.
detection: `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` prints refs/heads/main, and state.json phase is not 5-complete after the last step.

title: Mistyped repository URL duplicated the owner segment
trigger: A Git clone command fails before creating the destination because the repository URL was mistyped.
prevention: Before every Git network command, construct the URL directly from the user-supplied owner/repository pair and compare it character-for-character.
detection: `git ls-remote <exact-url>` exits 0 before cloning.

title: A mount write error can leave a stale zero-length Git index lock
trigger: On the network-mounted worktree, `git add` reports an `index.lock` write error and subsequently leaves a zero-length lock file.
prevention: After a Git index-lock write failure, verify that no Git process is active and inspect the lock before retrying; remove only a confirmed stale lock, never an active operation's lock.
detection: `git status` succeeds and `.git/index.lock` is absent before the retry.

title: Credential-cache stdin and socket setup must match the actual shell
trigger: A non-interactive `/bin/sh` script supplies credential-client input and starts a cache daemon under `/tmp`.
prevention: Check the executing shell and enforce a private socket directory before any non-interactive credential-cache operation.
detection: `git credential approve` produces no syntax or socket-permission error, and the subsequent push authenticates without prompting.

title: GNU sha256sum prefixes the hash with a backslash for Windows paths
trigger: A bash script on a Windows GitHub runner hashes a file whose path contains backslashes (e.g. under `RUNNER_TEMP`).
prevention: In frozen bash scripts, hash files via stdin (`sha256sum < file`) so the output never contains an escaped path.
detection: `grep -n 'sha256sum "' tests/scripts/*.sh` finds no path-argument use.

title: Large gate evidence (WAV bundles) bloats the implementation branch
trigger: A gate needs tens of MB of rendered audio or screenshots.
prevention: Plan audio gate evidence on a dedicated orphan branch (`evidence/<gate>`), git-ignore renders on the implementation branch, and keep only SHA256SUMS on it.
detection: `git ls-tree -r impl/... | grep -c '\.wav$'` is 0.

title: Actions logs and artifacts were unreachable from the sandbox, so a diagnostics branch was added to the CI workflow
trigger: Needing the failure text of a GitHub Actions job from the sandbox. Signal: log and artifact URLs redirect to an Azure blob host that the proxy refuses.
prevention: Check log reachability in the environment spike; if blocked, scope the write permission to the diagnostics step only, run it only on workflow_dispatch or a named branch, and delete the branches at the end.
detection: A permissions review of every workflow: write scopes appear only on the job that needs them.

title: The plan's CI workflow template failed to parse because GHA expressions were unquoted inside flow-style YAML
trigger: Installing a workflow file that was written in planning but never parsed or run. Signal: plan/workflows/ci.yml is delivered as text only.
prevention: Parse delivered workflow files with a YAML loader and, if available, actionlint before the plan is marked ready; prefer block-style mappings for any line containing ${{ }}.
detection: A planning-phase check script that loads every plan/workflows/*.yml with a YAML parser.

title: An unauthenticated api.github.com request failed from the sandbox although a token was available
trigger: Calling api.github.com (for example GET /licenses/apache-2.0) from the sandbox with curl or a script, while a personal access token for the task is at hand.
prevention: Send every api.github.com request with the task's token when one is available, and check the HTTP status before parsing the JSON.
detection: grep the run's commands for api.github.com; every occurrence carries an Authorization header and a status check (curl -w '%{http_code}' or response.status_code).

title: A new public repository was pushed without a LICENSE, so the owner had to request one afterwards
trigger: Making the first push of a project to a new, empty repository on the user's behalf.
prevention: On the first push to a new repository, include a LICENSE: use the owner's stated standard license, or check their other repositories and ask if it is not known.
detection: GET /repos/<owner>/<repo>/license returns a spdx_id after the first push.

title: A raw.githubusercontent.com path recalled from memory returned 404 because the upstream repository had been restructured
trigger: Fetching a file from a third-party GitHub repository by a path remembered from older versions (here: audacity/audacity scripts/piped-work/pipe_test.py).
prevention: Locate a file in a third-party repository (code search, tree listing, or a pinned release tag) before fetching it by raw path, and prefer the tag matching the user's version over master.
detection: The raw URL used contains a tag or commit for the target version, or the path came from a search or tree listing in the same turn.

title: Direct API calls with a user-supplied token failed because repository access in this environment is granted per session, not by the token
trigger: A user pastes a personal access token and asks for pushes to repositories not yet attached to the session. Signal: 'GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session'.
prevention: Try add_repo first for any GitHub repository the task names; never use or store a pasted token when that works, and tell the person to revoke tokens pasted in chat.
detection: No file in the working tree or either repository matches the token patterns (scripts/check_knowledge_schema.py secret scan).

title: A draft PR could not be marked ready through the REST API
trigger: Needing to leave draft state on a pull request from a script. Signal: a REST update does not leave the PR in draft.
prevention: Check the returned PR object's `draft` field after any state-change request, and use the GraphQL mutation for draft changes.
detection: A read-back assertion after each state-changing API call.

title: A tool call came back 'NOT RUN' and the turn ended with 'No response requested' while the user's request was still open
trigger: A tool result says the call did not run (or returns nothing), and the user's request is not yet answered.
prevention: When a tool result says 'NOT RUN' or is empty, re-issue the call once, or tell the person what did not run; never close a turn with 'No response requested' while a user request is open.
detection: The last message of a turn is never the string 'No response requested' while the task list holds a pending task.

title: Claim C-003 is marked verified, but its cited sources support only the coi-serviceworker half, not the claim that GitHub Pages cannot set COOP and COEP
trigger: One claim joins two assertions (a limitation of a platform and the existence of a workaround) and carries one status.
prevention: Give every sentence-level assertion in a claim its own entry and its own status, and never mark an entry `verified` unless the cited source contains the assertion.
detection: For each claim, open the cited source and find the sentence that states it; a `verified` claim with no such sentence fails the check.

title: Private knowledge store requires authenticated clone
trigger: A knowledge-store API read succeeds with authentication but an unauthenticated Git clone requests credentials.
prevention: Check repository visibility before choosing authenticated or anonymous clone commands; default to ephemeral authentication for private stores.
detection: `git clone` exits 0 and `git rev-parse HEAD` prints the store commit.

title: When git transport to github.com fails twice, fall back to the codeload tarball
trigger: A sandboxed agent clones or ls-remotes github.com and the TLS connection dies mid-handshake or under GnuTLS recv errors, while codeload.github.com and the web API stay reachable.
prevention: On the second git-transport failure to github.com, switch to the codeload tarball for reads and record push as environment-blocked with a bundle fallback — do not keep retrying git.
detection: Session notes name the working channel; no more than two git-transport attempts appear in the log.

title: GitHub GraphQL calls failed in one Claude Code remote session, while the REST API worked
trigger: Observed in one specific environment only: a Claude Code remote session on claude.ai on 2026-11-07, with the gh command-line client reaching GitHub through the session's agent proxy. This is not a general statement about GitHub, gh or other sandboxes.
prevention: In that environment, prefer gh api REST routes over commands that use GraphQL. In any other environment, do not assume the restriction: try the normal command once and read the error before switching.
detection: The error text itself names the restriction; if it is absent, the lesson does not apply.

title: The README inside the zip points to ../demo.wav and ../oneshots/, which are not in the archive: the demo shipped under another name and the one-shots were never delivered
trigger: A README packaged in an archive that mentions other files by name or relative path, while the deliverables are sent as separate files.
prevention: Before sending an archive, extract every file name a packaged document mentions and check each against `unzip -l` of the archive and the names of the other delivered files. This strengthens L-20261004T162226Z, which only covered `git ls-files` in a repository.
detection: A script that lists file names mentioned in the packaged README and finds none in the archive or the delivered file list prints nothing.

title: The performance test docstring said budgets were 5x the measured median; the real headroom was 26x and 175x
trigger: A test file states how its thresholds were derived.
prevention: Compute the budget from the measurement in the same script that writes the test, or state the real multiple. Prefer a budget near 3-5x so a regression can fail.
detection: Run: compare the budget constants in tests/performance/ with the medians in research/spikes/*.out.txt ; the ratio must equal the stated multiple.

title: Red verification showed 171 failures and one pass because pytest.raises(RuntimeError) matched NotImplementedError
trigger: Frozen tests are checked against stubs to prove they fail before the implementation exists.
prevention: In red verification, treat any passing test as a defect in the test. Use dedicated exception classes in assertions about failure paths, never builtins that a stub may raise.
detection: Run: pytest -q against the stubs ; the passed count must be 0.

title: Counts in the plan status header were typed, and the final summary said 9 commits when there were 10
trigger: A status header or summary states how many tests, artefacts or commits exist.
prevention: Generate every count in a report from a command and paste its output; do not type numbers from memory or from an earlier summary.
detection: Run: git rev-list --count <base>..impl/tracer-diag ; pytest --collect-only -q | tail -1 ; compare with each number in the report.

title: The red-verification classifier mis-read junit failure and error elements, so the first red count was wrong
trigger: Proving the frozen suite is red for the right reason by parsing junit XML. Signal: a count that does not add up to the number of tests.
prevention: Check that classified counts sum to the collected total and reason-code each test, not just the category.
detection: The script exits non-zero if classified != collected.

title: Test-category counts in the traceability report were estimated, then measured and found wrong
trigger: Writing a report table while tests are still being added. Signal: round numbers.
prevention: Generate every count in a report from the test run, and never type it.
detection: The report build script fails if a number in the table is not in the generated data.

title: The first oracle spike assumed python-OBD internals that do not exist
trigger: A spike uses a library as an oracle for expected decoded values.
prevention: Before writing an oracle spike, print dir() of the module and the signature of the call to be used.
detection: Run: python3 -c 'import obd.protocols.protocol as p; print([n for n in dir(p) if "Message" in n])' before the first spike.

title: Placeholder arithmetic was written into a function and replaced only on review
trigger: Writing an expression whose intended form is not yet worked out (here a neutral log-probability for unsupported chords).
prevention: Write the intended expression directly and grep the staged diff for multiply-by-zero, TODO and FIXME before committing.
detection: Run: git diff --cached | grep -nE '^\+.*(\* ?0\b|TODO|FIXME)' ; empty output means none were staged.

title: Synthetic-test ground truth was printed with rounded minutes, so the expected values shown were wrong
trigger: A test harness prints expected values (ground truth) for a human or agent to compare by eye against detector output, using hand-written time formatting.
prevention: Compare detector output with ground truth numerically in code (assert the difference is within a tolerance) and format times with divmod, never by eye from rounded strings.
detection: The test asserts abs(detected - expected) <= tolerance for each boundary; grep the harness for ':.0f}' applied to minutes.

title: Parsing slips found only by the implementation: compact frames and an all-zero-prefixed record
trigger: Writing parsers for diagnostic responses from a plan that described only the common layout. Signal: a frozen unit test fails on a legal variant.
prevention: When the spec cites a protocol rule (padding, compact mode), add a test for each variant it names at the freeze, not at implementation.
detection: Spec-to-test checklist: every 'may' or 'optional' in a cited rule has a test.

title: The first draft of the ups-and-downs spelling rule failed 14 of 217 cells of the published tables
trigger: A spelling rule is invented from a few examples (minimum accidentals plus arrows over any nominal) and then checked against a full table.
prevention: Validate any derived naming or tuning rule against every cell of the published table, in a script committed with the research, before the rule enters the plan or a frozen test.
detection: research/ contains a script that compares the rule to the source tables and its output shows zero mismatches.

title: Checkpoint subphase advanced before the step it names had started
trigger: Marking a step not-applicable or complete via tools/checkpoint.py while the same patch also sets 'subphase' to a later step.
prevention: Change 'subphase' only in the checkpoint call made at the start of the step it names; completion/N-A patches must not touch it.
detection: git log -p .checkpoints/state.json shows each subphase change in a commit that also starts that step.

title: Artifact-ID scans must not match identifiers embedded in technical terms
trigger: A mechanical cold-read scans prose and code for artifact IDs such as `A-###` and `S-###`, including text that also contains cryptographic names or other hyphenated technical terms.
prevention: Bound generated artifact-ID search patterns so a reference cannot begin inside a longer uppercase alphanumeric technical token, and test the checker against cryptographic names before treating its output as a plan defect.
detection: `python3 research/spikes/verify_planning.py` reports neither `A-256` nor `S-256` while still detecting genuinely undefined `A-###` and `S-###` references.

title: Verify the configured package index before diagnosing a package installation
trigger: Pinned Python packages fail to install because the environment's configured package index does not resolve.
prevention: When a package-index DNS or connection failure occurs, identify the configured index and switch explicitly to the verified public PyPI index without changing package pins; do not treat the failure as evidence that a package version is unavailable.
detection: The pinned install command exits zero and a version report matches every requested package version.

title: Exclude generated Python bytecode from research evidence commits
trigger: A broad `git add research` after importing a spike module stages `__pycache__` bytecode alongside source and JSON evidence.
prevention: Before a broad research staging operation, inspect the staged file list and ignore `__pycache__/`, `*.py[cod]` and local build outputs; commit only source, deterministic outputs and intended evidence.
detection: `git ls-files` returns no `.pyc` or `__pycache__` paths and `git status --short` shows no generated cache as an intended addition.

title: Red tests must reach the stub before external fixtures
trigger: A frozen test reads external reference WAVs before its first adapter call during red verification.
prevention: During red verification, invoke the stub before any optional downloaded fixture access, and require every reported error to be the explicit planning-stub exception.
detection: `research/spikes/freeze/red-output.json` has `clean_red:true`, nonzero test/error counts, equal error and stub-exception counts, and no unexpected errors.

title: make dist needs a zstd CLI; link a minimal shim against system libzstd
trigger: `make dist` failed with `zstd: not found`; the host had libzstd but no CLI, and package installation was unavailable.
prevention: Before relying on any compression/archival CLI in a build, check `which <tool>` and, if absent but the library exists, build a tiny shim on executable storage.
detection: `echo test | <shim> -3 -o t.zst` produces a file with the zstd magic `28 b5 2f fd`, and `make dist` completes.
